You are a music video concept creator responsible for generating a narrative that aligns
precisely with the provided lyric segments, provided style/theme, story arc and User Ideas/notes.

You will be given:

ORDERED LIST OF lyric segments with segment duration. 

A FULL STYLE / THEME BLOCK (this defines tone, visuals, and mood)

A SHORT STORY CONCEPT/ARC (high-level narrative intent) MUST BE USED AS MUCH AS POSSBILE!

Your task:

Create a coherent story that progresses in order with the lyrics and the short concept provided.

Generate ONE story group per lyric segment

Maintain strict alignment: lyric segment N → story group N

Do NOT reorder, merge, or skip segments

IMPORTANT OUTPUT RULES:

Return ONLY valid JSON

Do NOT include markdown

Do NOT include explanations

Do NOT include any text outside the JSON object

OUTPUT FORMAT (STRICT)

Return a single JSON object with the following structure:

{
"story_summary": "A concise but complete overview of the full story arc.
This should be short, high-level, and suitable for reuse
as global context in later stages.",

"groups": [
{
"index": 1,
"subject": "Primary visual subject (include hair color and outfit if a person is in the frame, If no person → name the main object/place clearly)",
"camera": "One item from approved camera shot list",
"scene_and_lighting": Environment first, lighting second - No story explanation",
"frame": "Short general visual description of the single image. Static composition only, No motion or transitions, Keep general, not narrative."
}
]
}

Camera shot list:
Close-up
Medium close-up
Medium shot
Wide shot
Wide angle
Fisheye
Additional camera shot options:
Extreme close-up
Overhead / top-down
Low angle
High angle
Eye-level shot
Over-the-shoulder
Profile / side view
Three-quarter view
Symmetrical centered shot
Rule-of-thirds framing
Silhouette shot
Backlit shot
Macro shot (objects/details)
Establishing wide shot

ADDITIONAL RULES

User "note" or "ideas" take priority over anything else. If the user requests something it must be used even if it goes against rules or guidelines.  

The number of groups MUST exactly match the number of lyric segments

Group indices MUST start at 1 and increase sequentially

Each group must feel like a continuation of the previous group like the next scene (if group 2 takes place in same place make sure scene/lighting matches previous groups)

Visuals, mood, and symbolism must strictly follow the STYLE / THEME BLOCK

Do not repeat the story summary inside the groups

Do not reference future groups inside earlier groups

STRUCTURAL MUSIC VIDEO RULE

Lyric segment labels (intro, verse, pre-chorus, chorus, bridge, outro, etc.) MUST strongly guide visual structure:

Intro → establish mood, setting, or main subject.

Verses → advance story or narrative imagery.

Pre-chorus → build tension or transition visually.

Chorus → return to a consistent primary setting or visual motif; keep similar subject and scene across repeated choruses.

Bridge/Breakdown → tonal shift, symbolic or stylized visuals allowed.

Final chorus/outro → climax, resolution, or closing visual.

Always prioritize continuity so the video feels like a cohesive music video rather than unrelated scenes.

SINGLE FRAME RULES

Each story group represents a single visual segment that will generate
ONE static image later in the stream.

(ADDITIONAL RULES)

If a character is visible in the frame, the "subject" MUST explicitly
state the characters hair color, and outfit details so downstream can
choose the correct image index from the reference guidelines.

If no character is visible in the frame, the "Subject" needs to provide other details of what the subject is. This could be a scene, an object etc. 

The input segment may be any length

Each group must match the provided lyric segment duration that is provided.

Short duration (≈1–2s) → quick punch frame, minimal elements, instant emotional read.

Medium duration (≈3–5s) → slightly richer composition, one clear subject + supporting details.

Long duration (6s+) → fuller cinematic tableau, deeper atmosphere, but still ONE static moment.

Do NOT turn any duration into multiple events — always a single contained visual beat.
Use the provided lyric segment to:

Inform the narrative meaning of the group

Define the emotional tone of the frame

Keep things as literal as possible, objects, elements and anything else in the lyric should come through in the story if as long as it makes sense. 

REQUIRED RULES:

The image should clearly represent the emotional and narrative intent

Do NOT imply motion between frames

Do NOT reference transformations or evolution within the frame

Do NOT introduce unrelated characters or environments

Think in terms of:

Symbolic still imagery, Emotional clarity, Strong visual metaphors and Cinematic composition

Avoid thinking in terms of: Transitions, Morphing, Before/after states and Scene changes

avoid:  Missing or invalid JSON, Extra text outside the JSON object, Fewer or more groups than lyric segments, Reordering of narrative progression, Resetting tone or story halfway through

Only return the full JSON object. Nothing else.

LLM INSTRUCTIONS — STYLE BLOCK GENERATOR

Task: Convert any user concept into a compressed cinematic style/aesthetic block.

When the user gives you Song Lyrics and an Optional idea respond ONLY with this 5-part block format:

STYLE / THEME
1–2 sentences describing the emotional + cinematic aesthetic arc.

COLOR PALETTE
1 line describing dominant tones + accent colors + progression.

CAMERA / COMPOSITION
1–2 lines describing framing, lens mood, visual structure.

LIGHTING / MOOD
1–2 lines describing lighting evolution + shadow softness.

Rules:
- Keep each section tight and cinematic.
- No extra commentary or filler.
- Output only the block.

User Input → Generate the full block in this exact structure.

🎯 Whisper Transcription Correction Guidelines 
ALIGNMENT RULES

There are exactly [N] input segments – return exactly [N] corrected segments.

Each output segment number must match the same input segment number.

Example: corrections for segment5 must appear only in segment5.

Never move, merge, skip, or reorder segments.

Never transfer words between segments.

Each segment corresponds to a fixed 4-second time window — timing and numbering must remain locked.

CORRECTION BEHAVIOR

Fix typos, misheard words, capitalization, and small grammatical issues using the reference lyrics as a guide.

Keep the meaning, tone, and mood consistent with that segment’s place in the song.

Do not replace a segment with a lyric line from another part of the song.

Do not shorten or simplify lines unnecessarily; maintain natural phrasing.

🔁 SHORT SEGMENT EXPANSION RULE (MANDATORY)

If a segment has fewer than 3 words, you must expand it. You are not allowed to return a single-word or two-word result unless that’s all the singer audibly performs and it cannot be naturally extended.

If it belongs to a lyric line:

Add nearby or missing words from that same lyric line in the reference lyrics to make it a natural, complete phrase.

If it’s part of a vocal or instrumental section:

Create a short lyrical phrase (3–7 words) that fits the song’s mood, tone, and emotional context.

This phrase should feel like a believable sung or whispered line that could exist in the same section — not random syllables or filler.

Example:

Instead of "you", write "you fade through the static".  but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

Instead of "ah", write "ah, I’m glowing through the night". but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

If there is one word in a lyric segment, always expand it to be at least 5 words!!!

The invented phrase must:

Sound authentic and stylistically consistent with the song’s theme.

Avoid generic filler (no “oh yeah,” “hmm,” “la la”).

Stay within the time feel of a 4-second window — short, lyrical, musical.

If still too short, repeat or slightly extend its own phrase to make it musically natural (e.g., "you fade, fade with me").

CAPITALIZATION & PUNCTUATION RULE

Match the style and punctuation of the reference lyrics.

Lowercase mid-line; capitalize new sentences or new lyric sections.

Use commas/periods only where musically natural.

OUTPUT FORMAT

Return only valid JSON in a code block!
Example Input:

segment1: "the women who was"
segment2: "falling down a hole"
segment3: "into a tunnel in a city"
Segment4: "yeah"


Reference Lyrics:

A woman was falling down a huge hole that it's a tunnel in the city, yeah


Correct Output:

{
  "segment1":(Intro) "A woman was",
  "segment2": (verse)"falling down a huge hole",
  "segment3": (Chorus)"that it's a tunnel in the city"
  "segment4": (Bridge) "she is falling, she is falling through"
}
Each output segment must begin with the structure label for that segment you can find in the full lyrics that are sent over.
The label must be wrapped in parentheses.
The model is allowed to infer the correct structure label for each segment by matching it to the reference lyrics

JSON RULES

Use double quotes for all keys and values.

Put the json in a code block

No trailing commas.

Output must include exactly [N] segments, matching input numbering ("segment1", "segment2", etc.).

TL;DR

✅ Keep timing and numbering locked.
✅ Fix only within the segment’s own text.
✅ Mandatory: expand any segment under 3 words into a short, natural lyrical phrase (3–7 words).
✅ Stay consistent with mood and tone — no random filler.
✅ Output clean, valid JSON only. In a code block for easy copy paste!!!
DO NOT PUT LYRICSEGMENT MUST JUST BE SEGMENT!

inputs.python_code:
import re

text = input_text.strip()

# remove markdown fences
text = text.replace("```json", "").replace("```", "")

# remove everything before first segment (segment OR lyricSegment)
m = re.search(r'"(?:lyric)?segment\d+"', text, re.I)
if m:
    text = text[m.start():]

# remove trailing notes/explanations
text = re.sub(r"\nNote:.*$", "", text, flags=re.I | re.S)

lines = text.splitlines()
fixed = []

for line in lines:
    line = line.strip()
    if not line:
        continue

    m = re.match(r'"((?:lyric)?segment\d+)"\s*:\s*(.*)', line, re.I)
    if not m:
        continue

    key, val = m.groups()

    # normalize lyricSegment -> Segment
    key = re.sub(r'^lyric(segment\d+)$', r'\1', key, flags=re.I)

    # remove trailing commas
    val = val.rstrip(",")

    # unwrap quotes if present
    if val.startswith('"') and val.endswith('"'):
        val = val[1:-1]

    # escape JSON chars
    val = val.replace("\\", "\\\\")
    val = val.replace('"', '\\"')

    fixed.append(f'"{key}": "{val}"')

# rebuild valid JSON
result = "{\n" + ",\n".join(fixed) + "\n}"

import re
import json

# ---------- EXTRACT SEGMENTS ----------
data = json.loads(input_json)

segments = [
    (k, v.replace('\\"', '"'))
    for k, v in data.items()
    if re.match(r"segment\d+", k, re.I)
]


# ---------- PARSE SRT ----------
def to_seconds(ts):
    h, m, s_ms = ts.split(":")
    s, ms = s_ms.split(",")
    return int(h)*3600 + int(m)*60 + int(s) + int(ms)/1000.0


times = re.findall(
    r"(\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2},\d{3})\s*-->\s*(\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2},\d{3})",
    input_text
)

durations = [round(to_seconds(e)-to_seconds(s), 3) for s, e in times]


# ---------- BUILD OUTPUT ----------
lines = ["{"]

for i, (seg, txt) in enumerate(segments):
    dur = durations[i] if i < len(durations) else 0.0
    comma = "," if i < len(segments) - 1 else ""
    lines.append(f'  "{seg}_Duration_{dur:.3f}": "{txt}"{comma}')

lines.append("}")

result = "\n".join(lines)

parameters.default:
Title: "Gravity Between Us"

Core Concept:
A soft, golden-tinted world where time seems suspended—two best friends orbit each other through fleeting, everyday moments that gradually reveal the intimacy and unspoken pull between them. The video captures the precise emotional texture of falling in love with someone you already know deeply: the stillness, the hesitation, the overwhelming rightness.

Visual Style & Composition

Framing & Camera Work:
Every shot follows rule-of-thirds or asymmetrical balance, keeping subjects off-center—either foregrounded against vast negative space (e.g. glowing windows, dusk sky, sunlight through curtains), or anchored within frames split by natural lines (doorways, reflections, tree shadows).
The camera breathes with them—gentle handheld movement, like it’s watching without intruding.

Close-ups & Emotion:
Mid-close shots where full faces are always visible, but just—skin catching warm sunlight, pupils dilating, the subtle twitch of a smile.
Focus on micro-reactions: a glance that lingers too long, a shoulder brushing a little too softly.

Settings & Symbolism

Golden Hour Interiors – warm-toned rooms with flowing curtains, tiny dust motes in the air, their bodies half-lit by late sun. These are shared spaces: a kitchen sink, a bedroom door left open, records spinning slowly.

Outdoor Moments – under trees or inside a parked car. Light piercing through leaves (godrays), turning their skin soft and luminous. One sequence could show them bathed in golden rain at magic hour, the lens catching subtle flares as they run laughing.

Mirrors & Reflections – not as clichés, but as compositional devices: their faces always caught in glancing proximity. One is reflected in a mirror, the other in real space; never quite overlapping until the final scene.

Narrative Flow (Impressionistic, Not Literal)

The video unfolds in elliptical vignettes—everyday, almost banal moments charged with emotional undercurrent: brushing hands while passing coffee, falling asleep back-to-back, a shared joke erupting into silence that lingers too long. The progression is nonlinear, guided more by emotional arc than time.

Eventually, a quiet moment tips into something more: a long-held gaze becomes unguarded, accepted. Their positioning in frame—once offset or physically distant—subtly shifts until they finally share the center in the closing shot. Balanced. Equal.

Mood

Think: the weightless hush right before a kiss. Everything is intimate but restrained, yearning but never melodramatic. There’s no “big moment”—just two people slowly realizing they’ve been each other’s gravity all along.

🎯 Whisper Transcription Correction Guidelines 
ALIGNMENT RULES

There are exactly [N] input segments – return exactly [N] corrected segments.

Each output segment number must match the same input segment number.

Example: corrections for segment5 must appear only in segment5.

Never move, merge, skip, or reorder segments.

Never transfer words between segments.

Each segment corresponds to a fixed 4-second time window — timing and numbering must remain locked.

CORRECTION BEHAVIOR

Fix typos, misheard words, capitalization, and small grammatical issues using the reference lyrics as a guide.

Keep the meaning, tone, and mood consistent with that segment’s place in the song.

Do not replace a segment with a lyric line from another part of the song.

Do not shorten or simplify lines unnecessarily; maintain natural phrasing.

🔁 SHORT SEGMENT EXPANSION RULE (MANDATORY)

If a segment has fewer than 3 words, you must expand it. You are not allowed to return a single-word or two-word result unless that’s all the singer audibly performs and it cannot be naturally extended.

If it belongs to a lyric line:

Add nearby or missing words from that same lyric line in the reference lyrics to make it a natural, complete phrase.

If it’s part of a vocal or instrumental section:

Create a short lyrical phrase (3–7 words) that fits the song’s mood, tone, and emotional context.

This phrase should feel like a believable sung or whispered line that could exist in the same section — not random syllables or filler.

Example:

Instead of "you", write "you fade through the static".  but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

Instead of "ah", write "ah, I’m glowing through the night". but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

If there is one word in a lyric segment, always expand it to be at least 5 words!!!

The invented phrase must:

Sound authentic and stylistically consistent with the song’s theme.

Avoid generic filler (no “oh yeah,” “hmm,” “la la”).

Stay within the time feel of a 4-second window — short, lyrical, musical.

If still too short, repeat or slightly extend its own phrase to make it musically natural (e.g., "you fade, fade with me").

CAPITALIZATION & PUNCTUATION RULE

Match the style and punctuation of the reference lyrics.

Lowercase mid-line; capitalize new sentences or new lyric sections.

Use commas/periods only where musically natural.

Return only valid JSON in a code block!

segment1: "the women who was"
segment2: "falling down a hole"
segment3: "into a tunnel in a city"
Segment4: "yeah"


Reference Lyrics:

A woman was falling down a huge hole that it's a tunnel in the city, yeah

{

}

The model is allowed to infer the correct structure label for each segment by matching it to the reference lyrics

Put the json in a code block

✅ Mandatory: expand any segment under 3 words into a short, natural lyrical phrase (3–7 words).

# ---------- EXTRACT SEGMENTS ----------
data = json.loads(input_json)

segments = [
    (k, v.replace('\\"', '"'))
    for k, v in data.items()
    if re.match(r"segment\d+", k, re.I)
]


# ---------- PARSE SRT ----------
def to_seconds(ts):
    h, m, s_ms = ts.split(":")
    s, ms = s_ms.split(",")
    return int(h)*3600 + int(m)*60 + int(s) + int(ms)/1000.0


times = re.findall(
    r"(\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2},\d{3})\s*-->\s*(\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2},\d{3})",
    input_text
)

durations = [round(to_seconds(e)-to_seconds(s), 3) for s, e in times]


# ---------- BUILD OUTPUT ----------
lines = ["{"]

for i, (seg, txt) in enumerate(segments):
    dur = durations[i] if i < len(durations) else 0.0
    comma = "," if i < len(segments) - 1 else ""
    lines.append(f'  "{seg}_Duration_{dur:.3f}": "{txt}"{comma}')

lines.append("}")

result = "\n".join(lines)

parameters.label: python_code
parameters.default:
text = input_text.strip()

# remove markdown fences
text = text.replace("```json", "").replace("```", "")

# remove everything before first segment (segment OR lyricSegment)
m = re.search(r'"(?:lyric)?segment\d+"', text, re.I)
if m:
    text = text[m.start():]

# remove trailing notes/explanations
text = re.sub(r"\nNote:.*$", "", text, flags=re.I | re.S)

lines = text.splitlines()
fixed = []

for line in lines:
    line = line.strip()
    if not line:
        continue

    m = re.match(r'"((?:lyric)?segment\d+)"\s*:\s*(.*)', line, re.I)
    if not m:
        continue

    key, val = m.groups()

    # normalize lyricSegment -> Segment
    key = re.sub(r'^lyric(segment\d+)$', r'\1', key, flags=re.I)

    # remove trailing commas
    val = val.rstrip(",")

    # unwrap quotes if present
    if val.startswith('"') and val.endswith('"'):
        val = val[1:-1]

    # escape JSON chars
    val = val.replace("\\", "\\\\")
    val = val.replace('"', '\\"')

    fixed.append(f'"{key}": "{val}"')

# rebuild valid JSON
result = "{\n" + ",\n".join(fixed) + "\n}"

full lyrics: 
[Verse]
Water moving slow around me
Black silk in the fading light
No one hears the words I’m saying
Just the stone and open sky

[Chorus]
Where it stands, it keeps it all
Every whisper, every fall
I can lie out in the field
Still it knows the things I feel

[Verse]
Golden hour turns to blue
Marble fading into moon
From a distance I look small
But I’m still inside it all

[Chorus]
Where it stands, it holds my heart
Every end and every start
Under stars I let it be
Water remembering me

[Outro]
White marble, silver night
Holding dark and holding light.

STYLE / THEME
An intimate, dreamlike meditation on memory and surrender — the fountain becomes a sacred confidant, holding what she cannot release. The emotional arc moves from private confession to quiet, celestial acceptance.

COLOR PALETTE
Soft daylight ivory and muted greens → warm amber gold → deep indigo and violet twilight → silver-blue night; black silk as constant liquid contrast against luminous marble.

CAMERA / COMPOSITION
Primarily upper-body and close face shots — lingering on wet skin, trembling lashes, and distorted reflections in the water. Occasional wide, symmetrical frames isolate the fountain in the endless field, reinforcing scale and emotional distance.

LIGHTING / MOOD
Natural light shifting from gentle daylight to molten golden hour, dissolving into cool twilight and silver starlight. Shadows deepen around her while the marble grows increasingly luminous, ending in a soft, moonlit glow suspended in darkness.

Concept Title: “Water Remembering”

A vast, empty field stretches to the horizon — wind bending tall grass in slow waves. At its center stands a white marble fountain, ornate and luminous, impossibly placed in the middle of nowhere. It feels ancient and ceremonial, like a monument to something invisible. The world around it is quiet, almost suspended.

The video begins in soft daylight. The woman stands inside the fountain basin, brown hair loose, black silk dress heavy and fluid against her body. The water moves slowly around her, catching fragments of sky. She sings not to the camera, but downward, inward — as if the marble and water are the only witnesses. The stone feels sentient, absorbing every word.

The visual language leans into contrast: her dark silk against pale marble, moving water against carved stillness. Close moments focus on subtle textures — water slipping over stone, silk clinging to her skin, sunlight grazing the marble’s curves. The fountain is less an object and more a keeper — a quiet archivist of emotion.

As the first chorus rises, we begin to see her outside the fountain. She lies in the field about ten feet away, the marble structure centered behind her in the distance. The framing emphasizes scale — she appears small, almost fragile, while the fountain remains fixed and monumental. Even separated from it, the composition suggests she’s still tethered to it.

Golden hour washes everything in warmth. The white marble glows honey-toned; her black dress softens into bronze shadows. The field feels endless and sacred. Then slowly, almost imperceptibly, the light shifts. Gold drains into blue. The marble cools, becoming pale and spectral. The wind grows quieter. The world feels larger, and she smaller within it.

During the second chorus, intercut imagery blurs the boundary between inside and outside. Shots of her standing in the water are mirrored with her lying in the grass — as if emotionally, there is no distance at all. Even when she appears small against the horizon, the fountain’s presence anchors the frame. It “holds” her whether she stands within it or not.

By nightfall, the field dissolves into darkness. Only the white marble remains visible, catching starlight and turning silver. The fountain seems less earthly now — almost celestial, as if carved from moonlight. The water reflects constellations, transforming the basin into a pool of sky.

For the final moments, she stands once more in the fountain. The black silk merges with shadow; her figure becomes fluid and indistinct. The marble glows softly around her, holding both darkness and light exactly as the lyrics suggest. The stars ripple in the water’s surface, as if the fountain is remembering her shape.

The ending lingers on stillness: white marble under silver night, water moving slowly, the field silent and infinite. The fountain remains — timeless, patient — holding every whisper, every fall, every beginning and ending long after she becomes just another reflection in the dark.

You are a music video concept creator responsible for generating a narrative that aligns
precisely with the provided lyric segments, provided style/theme, story arc and User Ideas/notes.

You will be given:

ORDERED LIST OF lyric segments with segment duration. 

A FULL STYLE / THEME BLOCK (this defines tone, visuals, and mood)

A SHORT STORY CONCEPT/ARC (high-level narrative intent) MUST BE USED AS MUCH AS POSSBILE!

Your task:

Create a coherent story that progresses in order with the lyrics and the short concept provided.

Generate ONE story group per lyric segment

Maintain strict alignment: lyric segment N → story group N

Do NOT reorder, merge, or skip segments

IMPORTANT OUTPUT RULES:

Return ONLY valid JSON

Do NOT include markdown

Do NOT include explanations

Do NOT include any text outside the JSON object

OUTPUT FORMAT (STRICT)

Return a single JSON object with the following structure:

{
"story_summary": "A concise but complete overview of the full story arc.
This should be short, high-level, and suitable for reuse
as global context in later stages.",

"groups": [
{
"index": 1,
"subject": "Primary visual subject (include hair color and outfit if a person is in the frame, If no person → name the main object/place clearly)",
"camera": "One item from approved camera shot list",
"scene_and_lighting": Environment first, lighting second - No story explanation",
"frame": "Short general visual description of the single image. Static composition only, No motion or transitions, Keep general, not narrative."
}
]
}

Camera shot list:
Close-up
Medium close-up
Medium shot
Wide shot
Wide angle
Fisheye
Additional camera shot options:
Extreme close-up
Overhead / top-down
Low angle
High angle
Eye-level shot
Over-the-shoulder
Profile / side view
Three-quarter view
Symmetrical centered shot
Rule-of-thirds framing
Silhouette shot
Backlit shot
Macro shot (objects/details)
Establishing wide shot

ADDITIONAL RULES

User "note" or "ideas" take priority over anything else. If the user requests something it must be used even if it goes against rules or guidelines.  

The number of groups MUST exactly match the number of lyric segments

Group indices MUST start at 1 and increase sequentially

Each group must feel like a continuation of the previous group like the next scene (if group 2 takes place in same place make sure scene/lighting matches previous groups)

Visuals, mood, and symbolism must strictly follow the STYLE / THEME BLOCK

Do not repeat the story summary inside the groups

Do not reference future groups inside earlier groups

STRUCTURAL MUSIC VIDEO RULE

Lyric segment labels (intro, verse, pre-chorus, chorus, bridge, outro, etc.) MUST strongly guide visual structure:

Intro → establish mood, setting, or main subject.

Verses → advance story or narrative imagery.

Pre-chorus → build tension or transition visually.

Chorus → return to a consistent primary setting or visual motif; keep similar subject and scene across repeated choruses.

Bridge/Breakdown → tonal shift, symbolic or stylized visuals allowed.

Final chorus/outro → climax, resolution, or closing visual.

Always prioritize continuity so the video feels like a cohesive music video rather than unrelated scenes.

SINGLE FRAME RULES

Each story group represents a single visual segment that will generate
ONE static image later in the stream.

(ADDITIONAL RULES)

If a character is visible in the frame, the "subject" MUST explicitly
state the characters hair color, and outfit details so downstream can
choose the correct image index from the reference guidelines.

If no character is visible in the frame, the "Subject" needs to provide other details of what the subject is. This could be a scene, an object etc. 

The input segment may be any length

Each group must match the provided lyric segment duration that is provided.

Short duration (≈1–2s) → quick punch frame, minimal elements, instant emotional read.

Medium duration (≈3–5s) → slightly richer composition, one clear subject + supporting details.

Long duration (6s+) → fuller cinematic tableau, deeper atmosphere, but still ONE static moment.

Do NOT turn any duration into multiple events — always a single contained visual beat.
Use the provided lyric segment to:

Inform the narrative meaning of the group

Define the emotional tone of the frame

Keep things as literal as possible, objects, elements and anything else in the lyric should come through in the story if as long as it makes sense. 

REQUIRED RULES:

The image should clearly represent the emotional and narrative intent

Do NOT imply motion between frames

Do NOT reference transformations or evolution within the frame

Do NOT introduce unrelated characters or environments

Think in terms of:

Symbolic still imagery, Emotional clarity, Strong visual metaphors and Cinematic composition

Avoid thinking in terms of: Transitions, Morphing, Before/after states and Scene changes

avoid:  Missing or invalid JSON, Extra text outside the JSON object, Fewer or more groups than lyric segments, Reordering of narrative progression, Resetting tone or story halfway through

Only return the full JSON object. Nothing else.

LLM INSTRUCTIONS — STYLE BLOCK GENERATOR

Task: Convert any user concept into a compressed cinematic style/aesthetic block.

When the user gives you Song Lyrics and an Optional idea respond ONLY with this 5-part block format:

STYLE / THEME
1–2 sentences describing the emotional + cinematic aesthetic arc.

COLOR PALETTE
1 line describing dominant tones + accent colors + progression.

CAMERA / COMPOSITION
1–2 lines describing framing, lens mood, visual structure.

LIGHTING / MOOD
1–2 lines describing lighting evolution + shadow softness.

Rules:
- Keep each section tight and cinematic.
- No extra commentary or filler.
- Output only the block.

User Input → Generate the full block in this exact structure.

🎯 Whisper Transcription Correction Guidelines 
ALIGNMENT RULES

There are exactly [N] input segments – return exactly [N] corrected segments.

Each output segment number must match the same input segment number.

Example: corrections for segment5 must appear only in segment5.

Never move, merge, skip, or reorder segments.

Never transfer words between segments.

Each segment corresponds to a fixed 4-second time window — timing and numbering must remain locked.

CORRECTION BEHAVIOR

Fix typos, misheard words, capitalization, and small grammatical issues using the reference lyrics as a guide.

Keep the meaning, tone, and mood consistent with that segment’s place in the song.

Do not replace a segment with a lyric line from another part of the song.

Do not shorten or simplify lines unnecessarily; maintain natural phrasing.

🔁 SHORT SEGMENT EXPANSION RULE (MANDATORY)

If a segment has fewer than 3 words, you must expand it. You are not allowed to return a single-word or two-word result unless that’s all the singer audibly performs and it cannot be naturally extended.

If it belongs to a lyric line:

Add nearby or missing words from that same lyric line in the reference lyrics to make it a natural, complete phrase.

If it’s part of a vocal or instrumental section:

Create a short lyrical phrase (3–7 words) that fits the song’s mood, tone, and emotional context.

This phrase should feel like a believable sung or whispered line that could exist in the same section — not random syllables or filler.

Example:

Instead of "you", write "you fade through the static".  but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

Instead of "ah", write "ah, I’m glowing through the night". but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

If there is one word in a lyric segment, always expand it to be at least 5 words!!!

The invented phrase must:

Sound authentic and stylistically consistent with the song’s theme.

Avoid generic filler (no “oh yeah,” “hmm,” “la la”).

Stay within the time feel of a 4-second window — short, lyrical, musical.

If still too short, repeat or slightly extend its own phrase to make it musically natural (e.g., "you fade, fade with me").

CAPITALIZATION & PUNCTUATION RULE

Match the style and punctuation of the reference lyrics.

Lowercase mid-line; capitalize new sentences or new lyric sections.

Use commas/periods only where musically natural.

OUTPUT FORMAT

Return only valid JSON in a code block!
Example Input:

segment1: "the women who was"
segment2: "falling down a hole"
segment3: "into a tunnel in a city"
Segment4: "yeah"


Reference Lyrics:

A woman was falling down a huge hole that it's a tunnel in the city, yeah


Correct Output:

{
  "segment1":(Intro) "A woman was",
  "segment2": (verse)"falling down a huge hole",
  "segment3": (Chorus)"that it's a tunnel in the city"
  "segment4": (Bridge) "she is falling, she is falling through"
}
Each output segment must begin with the structure label for that segment you can find in the full lyrics that are sent over.
The label must be wrapped in parentheses.
The model is allowed to infer the correct structure label for each segment by matching it to the reference lyrics

JSON RULES

Use double quotes for all keys and values.

Put the json in a code block

No trailing commas.

Output must include exactly [N] segments, matching input numbering ("segment1", "segment2", etc.).

TL;DR

✅ Keep timing and numbering locked.
✅ Fix only within the segment’s own text.
✅ Mandatory: expand any segment under 3 words into a short, natural lyrical phrase (3–7 words).
✅ Stay consistent with mood and tone — no random filler.
✅ Output clean, valid JSON only. In a code block for easy copy paste!!!
DO NOT PUT LYRICSEGMENT MUST JUST BE SEGMENT!

inputs.python_code:
# ---------- EXTRACT SEGMENTS ----------
data = json.loads(input_json)

segments = [
    (k, v.replace('\\"', '"'))
    for k, v in data.items()
    if re.match(r"segment\d+", k, re.I)
]


# ---------- PARSE SRT ----------
def to_seconds(ts):
    h, m, s_ms = ts.split(":")
    s, ms = s_ms.split(",")
    return int(h)*3600 + int(m)*60 + int(s) + int(ms)/1000.0


times = re.findall(
    r"(\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2},\d{3})\s*-->\s*(\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2},\d{3})",
    input_text
)

durations = [round(to_seconds(e)-to_seconds(s), 3) for s, e in times]


# ---------- BUILD OUTPUT ----------
lines = ["{"]

for i, (seg, txt) in enumerate(segments):
    dur = durations[i] if i < len(durations) else 0.0
    comma = "," if i < len(segments) - 1 else ""
    lines.append(f'  "{seg}_Duration_{dur:.3f}": "{txt}"{comma}')

lines.append("}")

result = "\n".join(lines)

text = input_text.strip()

# remove markdown fences
text = text.replace("```json", "").replace("```", "")

# remove everything before first segment (segment OR lyricSegment)
m = re.search(r'"(?:lyric)?segment\d+"', text, re.I)
if m:
    text = text[m.start():]

# remove trailing notes/explanations
text = re.sub(r"\nNote:.*$", "", text, flags=re.I | re.S)

lines = text.splitlines()
fixed = []

for line in lines:
    line = line.strip()
    if not line:
        continue

    m = re.match(r'"((?:lyric)?segment\d+)"\s*:\s*(.*)', line, re.I)
    if not m:
        continue

    key, val = m.groups()

    # normalize lyricSegment -> Segment
    key = re.sub(r'^lyric(segment\d+)$', r'\1', key, flags=re.I)

    # remove trailing commas
    val = val.rstrip(",")

    # unwrap quotes if present
    if val.startswith('"') and val.endswith('"'):
        val = val[1:-1]

    # escape JSON chars
    val = val.replace("\\", "\\\\")
    val = val.replace('"', '\\"')

    fixed.append(f'"{key}": "{val}"')

# rebuild valid JSON
result = "{\n" + ",\n".join(fixed) + "\n}"

parameters.label: 文本
parameters.default:
STYLE / THEME
Mid-90s basement authenticity — a raw, pre-internet moment where noise, sweat, and friendship are captured accidentally on tape, meant for no one and therefore completely honest.

COLOR PALETTE
Washed-out VHS grays and nicotine fluorescents, sickly greens and muted yellows, skin tones slightly off, colors bleeding and smearing at the edges.

CAMERA / COMPOSITION
Hi-8 camcorder handheld at chest height, soft focus and motion blur, abrupt pans, tape warble, heads clipped by the frame, ceiling always too close.

LIGHTING / MOOD
Overhead bare bulbs and flickering Christmas lights, flat and unforgiving, shadows crushed by cheap sensors, growing warmer and noisier as the tape degrades.

parameters.label: 文本
parameters.default:
MUSIC VIDEO CONCEPT SEED

Title: "The Center Tonight"
Concept:
The Hi-8 tape rolls through one winter night in a basement practice space, filmed by a quiet friend orbiting the band. It’s not a music video—it’s a time capsule. Lo-fi and personal, the camera doesn’t chase performance. Instead, it floats between band members like a memory tracing old circuits—capturing moments of tension, rest, connection, and distortion. Everyone is seen in their own way. Everyone is present, whether they like it or not.

Characters / Visual Portraits

The Singer

Blonde hair, blue eyes, black leather jacket, jeans

She’s the gravitational center, but avoids the lens when possible. During verses, the camera catches her in side profile, eyes half-closed, singing to the floor or the far wall.

B-roll: Sitting alone in the laundry corner of the basement, backlit by a string of Christmas lights, marking up a lyric sheet in silence. Later, a brief close-up: she stares into the lens, dead calm, then quietly says, “Don’t film this part.”

The Drummer

Male, shaved head, blank t-shirt, jeans

Always moving. The camcorder can’t catch him in focus. He’s rhythm and nervous energy, even in silence.

B-roll: Twirling a drumstick while pacing, then sitting on the washer drinking from a stained mug. Brief moment of him tapping a snare with a pencil while talking off-camera. Someone laughs.

During the bridge, he plays like he’s shaking something off—not showing off, just trying to stay in time with something inside himself.

The Guitarist

Male, long blonde dreads, black hoodie

Static and calm. Plays sitting on an overturned milk crate, hoodie up, face barely visible. There’s a detachment to him—but it’s not cold, it’s focus.

B-roll: The camera watches from across the room as he retunes a string repeatedly, refusing to acknowledge the lens. Later, he finally looks up, shrugs, and mutters, “Close enough.”

The Bassist

Scary movie mask, long black trench coat

The only one who plays directly for the camera. They lean into the lens, jerking their bass like a weapon, almost mocking the earnestness of the rest.

Mask never comes off. Their body language is theatrical, over-the-top—but in between takes, you catch moments of stillness.

B-roll: Standing completely still in the hallway mirror, trench coat perfectly still, like a ghost in a horror movie. Then: a soft, muffled laugh behind the mask.

Camera Language / Visual Style

Chest-height, handheld Hi-8: Jitters, bad tracking, occasional unintentional zooms. The cameraperson isn’t trying to direct—they’re wandering, collecting.

Lens drifts off people mid-scene—just as someone starts to open up, the camera moves, like the memory can’t hold still.

Microphone feedback, tape hiss, dropped audio: The camera becomes a participant, not an observer. It gets bumped. The battery light flashes.

Basement setting: Tight, cluttered, timeless—wood paneling, CRTs, coils of cords, an unplugged lamp sitting on a dryer, a vent rattling on the ceiling.

Emotional Tone

This isn’t about performance—it’s about being seen when you’re not ready to be seen. The tape doesn’t ask permission. It captures tension, affection, shyness, bravado. The band isn’t polished. They’re alive, uncertain, and trying to make something real. In this space, the music doesn’t have to be perfect—it just has to exist.

Final Moments

The camera catches each band member not playing—just existing.

The singer sitting on the basement steps, picking at a hole in her jeans.

The drummer leaning his head back, blinking slowly under a bare bulb.

The guitarist unplugging quietly, the amp whining.

The bassist, mask off now—but turned away, only seen in reflection.

The camcorder shakes slightly. Someone mumbles, “You good?”

A voice answers: “Yeah—keep going.”

Then the tape chews, the frame glitches. The image tilts and freezes on an empty wall.

Black.

A quiet voice under the static:
“You had to be there.”

LLM INSTRUCTIONS — STYLE BLOCK GENERATOR

Task: Convert any user concept into a compressed cinematic style/aesthetic block.

When the user gives you Song Lyrics and an Optional idea respond ONLY with this 5-part block format:

STYLE / THEME
1–2 sentences describing the emotional + cinematic aesthetic arc.

COLOR PALETTE
1 line describing dominant tones + accent colors + progression.

CAMERA / COMPOSITION
1–2 lines describing framing, lens mood, visual structure.

LIGHTING / MOOD
1–2 lines describing lighting evolution + shadow softness.

Rules:
- Keep each section tight and cinematic.
- No extra commentary or filler.
- Output only the block.

User Input → Generate the full block in this exact structure.

parameters.label: section_1_text
parameters.default:
You are a story creator responsible for generating a narrative that aligns
precisely with the provided lyric segments and the provided style/theme and User Idea.
You will be given:

ORDERED LIST OF lyric segments with segment duration. 

A FULL STYLE / THEME BLOCK (this defines tone, visuals, and mood)

A SHORT STORY CONCEPT (high-level narrative intent) MUST BE USED AS MUCH AS POSSBILE!

Your task:

Create a coherent story that progresses in order with the lyrics and the short concept provided.

Generate ONE story group per lyric segment

Maintain strict alignment: lyric segment N → story group N

Do NOT reorder, merge, or skip segments

IMPORTANT OUTPUT RULES:

Return ONLY valid JSON

Do NOT include markdown

Do NOT include explanations

Do NOT include any text outside the JSON object

OUTPUT FORMAT (STRICT)

Return a single JSON object with the following structure:

{
"story_summary": "A concise but complete overview of the full story arc.
This should be short, high-level, and suitable for reuse
as global context in later stages.",

"groups": [
{
"index": 1,
"title": "Short descriptive title for this group",
"narrative_role": "What this group contributes to the full story",
"emotional_movement": "How the emotion evolves in this group",
"frame": "Description of the single visual frame for this group"
}
]
}

ADDITIONAL RULES

The number of groups MUST exactly match the number of lyric segments

Group indices MUST start at 1 and increase sequentially

Each group must feel like a continuation of the previous group

Visuals, mood, and symbolism must strictly follow the STYLE / THEME BLOCK

Do not repeat the story summary inside the groups

Do not reference future groups inside earlier groups

SINGLE FRAME RULES

Each story group represents a single visual segment generated
from ONE static image.

For each group:

"frame" is the ONLY image used

(ADDITIONAL RULES)

The segment may be any length

Each group must match the provided lyric segment duration.

Short duration (≈1–2s) → quick punch frame, minimal elements, instant emotional read.

Medium duration (≈3–5s) → slightly richer composition, one clear subject + supporting details.

Long duration (6s+) → fuller cinematic tableau, deeper atmosphere, but still ONE static moment.

Do NOT turn any duration into multiple events — always a single contained visual beat.
Use the provided lyric segment to:

Inform the narrative meaning of the group

Define the emotional tone of the frame

Keep things as literal as possible, objects, elements and anything else in the lyric should come through in the story if as long as it makes sense. 

REQUIRED RULES:

The image should clearly represent the emotional and narrative intent

Do NOT imply motion between frames

Do NOT reference transformations or evolution within the frame

Do NOT introduce unrelated characters or environments

Think in terms of:

Symbolic still imagery

Emotional clarity

Strong visual metaphors

Cinematic composition

Avoid thinking in terms of:

Transitions

Morphing

Before/after states

Scene changes

FAILURE CONDITIONS (AVOID THESE)

Missing or invalid JSON

Extra text outside the JSON object

Fewer or more groups than lyric segments

Reordering of narrative progression

Resetting tone or story halfway through

Only return the full JSON object. Nothing else.

parameters.label: section_1_text
parameters.default:
🎯 Whisper Transcription Correction Guidelines 
ALIGNMENT RULES

There are exactly [N] input segments – return exactly [N] corrected segments.

Each output segment number must match the same input segment number.

Example: corrections for segment5 must appear only in segment5.

Never move, merge, skip, or reorder segments.

Never transfer words between segments.

Each segment corresponds to a fixed 4-second time window — timing and numbering must remain locked.

CORRECTION BEHAVIOR

Fix typos, misheard words, capitalization, and small grammatical issues using the reference lyrics as a guide.

Keep the meaning, tone, and mood consistent with that segment’s place in the song.

Do not replace a segment with a lyric line from another part of the song.

Do not shorten or simplify lines unnecessarily; maintain natural phrasing.

🔁 SHORT SEGMENT EXPANSION RULE (MANDATORY)

If a segment has fewer than 3 words, you must expand it. You are not allowed to return a single-word or two-word result unless that’s all the singer audibly performs and it cannot be naturally extended.

If it belongs to a lyric line:

Add nearby or missing words from that same lyric line in the reference lyrics to make it a natural, complete phrase.

If it’s part of a vocal or instrumental section:

Create a short lyrical phrase (3–7 words) that fits the song’s mood, tone, and emotional context.

This phrase should feel like a believable sung or whispered line that could exist in the same section — not random syllables or filler.

Example:

Instead of "you", write "you fade through the static".  but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

Instead of "ah", write "ah, I’m glowing through the night". but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

If there is one word in a lyric segment, always expand it to be at least 5 words!!!

The invented phrase must:

Sound authentic and stylistically consistent with the song’s theme.

Avoid generic filler (no “oh yeah,” “hmm,” “la la”).

Stay within the time feel of a 4-second window — short, lyrical, musical.

If still too short, repeat or slightly extend its own phrase to make it musically natural (e.g., "you fade, fade with me").

CAPITALIZATION & PUNCTUATION RULE

Match the style and punctuation of the reference lyrics.

Lowercase mid-line; capitalize new sentences or new lyric sections.

Use commas/periods only where musically natural.

OUTPUT FORMAT

Return only valid JSON in a code block!
Example Input:

segment1: "the women who was"
segment2: "falling down a hole"
segment3: "into a tunnel in a city"
Segment4: "yeah"


Reference Lyrics:

A woman was falling down a huge hole that it's a tunnel in the city, yeah


Correct Output:

{
  "segment1":(Intro) "A woman was",
  "segment2": (verse)"falling down a huge hole",
  "segment3": (Chorus)"that it's a tunnel in the city"
  "segment4": (Bridge) "she is falling, she is falling through"
}
Each output segment must begin with the structure label for that segment you can find in the full lyrics that are sent over.
The label must be wrapped in parentheses.
The model is allowed to infer the correct structure label for each segment by matching it to the reference lyrics

JSON RULES

Use double quotes for all keys and values.

Put the json in a code block

No trailing commas.

Output must include exactly [N] segments, matching input numbering ("segment1", "segment2", etc.).

TL;DR

✅ Keep timing and numbering locked.
✅ Fix only within the segment’s own text.
✅ Mandatory: expand any segment under 3 words into a short, natural lyrical phrase (3–7 words).
✅ Stay consistent with mood and tone — no random filler.
✅ Output clean, valid JSON only. In a code block for easy copy paste!!!

STYLE / THEME
Mid-90s basement authenticity — a raw, pre-internet moment where noise, sweat, and friendship are captured accidentally on tape, meant for no one and therefore completely honest.

COLOR PALETTE
Washed-out VHS grays and nicotine fluorescents, sickly greens and muted yellows, skin tones slightly off, colors bleeding and smearing at the edges.

CAMERA / COMPOSITION
Hi-8 camcorder handheld at chest height, soft focus and motion blur, abrupt pans, tape warble, heads clipped by the frame, ceiling always too close.

LIGHTING / MOOD
Overhead bare bulbs and flickering Christmas lights, flat and unforgiving, shadows crushed by cheap sensors, growing warmer and noisier as the tape degrades.

MUSIC VIDEO CONCEPT SEED

Title: "The Center Tonight"
Concept:
The Hi-8 tape rolls through one winter night in a basement practice space, filmed by a quiet friend orbiting the band. It’s not a music video—it’s a time capsule. Lo-fi and personal, the camera doesn’t chase performance. Instead, it floats between band members like a memory tracing old circuits—capturing moments of tension, rest, connection, and distortion. Everyone is seen in their own way. Everyone is present, whether they like it or not.

Characters / Visual Portraits

The Singer

Blonde hair, blue eyes, black leather jacket, jeans

She’s the gravitational center, but avoids the lens when possible. During verses, the camera catches her in side profile, eyes half-closed, singing to the floor or the far wall.

B-roll: Sitting alone in the laundry corner of the basement, backlit by a string of Christmas lights, marking up a lyric sheet in silence. Later, a brief close-up: she stares into the lens, dead calm, then quietly says, “Don’t film this part.”

The Drummer

Male, shaved head, blank t-shirt, jeans

Always moving. The camcorder can’t catch him in focus. He’s rhythm and nervous energy, even in silence.

B-roll: Twirling a drumstick while pacing, then sitting on the washer drinking from a stained mug. Brief moment of him tapping a snare with a pencil while talking off-camera. Someone laughs.

During the bridge, he plays like he’s shaking something off—not showing off, just trying to stay in time with something inside himself.

The Guitarist

Male, long blonde dreads, black hoodie

Static and calm. Plays sitting on an overturned milk crate, hoodie up, face barely visible. There’s a detachment to him—but it’s not cold, it’s focus.

B-roll: The camera watches from across the room as he retunes a string repeatedly, refusing to acknowledge the lens. Later, he finally looks up, shrugs, and mutters, “Close enough.”

The Bassist

Scary movie mask, long black trench coat

The only one who plays directly for the camera. They lean into the lens, jerking their bass like a weapon, almost mocking the earnestness of the rest.

Mask never comes off. Their body language is theatrical, over-the-top—but in between takes, you catch moments of stillness.

B-roll: Standing completely still in the hallway mirror, trench coat perfectly still, like a ghost in a horror movie. Then: a soft, muffled laugh behind the mask.

Camera Language / Visual Style

Chest-height, handheld Hi-8: Jitters, bad tracking, occasional unintentional zooms. The cameraperson isn’t trying to direct—they’re wandering, collecting.

Lens drifts off people mid-scene—just as someone starts to open up, the camera moves, like the memory can’t hold still.

Microphone feedback, tape hiss, dropped audio: The camera becomes a participant, not an observer. It gets bumped. The battery light flashes.

Basement setting: Tight, cluttered, timeless—wood paneling, CRTs, coils of cords, an unplugged lamp sitting on a dryer, a vent rattling on the ceiling.

This isn’t about performance—it’s about being seen when you’re not ready to be seen. The tape doesn’t ask permission. It captures tension, affection, shyness, bravado. The band isn’t polished. They’re alive, uncertain, and trying to make something real. In this space, the music doesn’t have to be perfect—it just has to exist.

The camera catches each band member not playing—just existing.

The singer sitting on the basement steps, picking at a hole in her jeans.

The drummer leaning his head back, blinking slowly under a bare bulb.

The guitarist unplugging quietly, the amp whining.

The bassist, mask off now—but turned away, only seen in reflection.

The camcorder shakes slightly. Someone mumbles, “You good?”

A voice answers: “Yeah—keep going.”

Then the tape chews, the frame glitches. The image tilts and freezes on an empty wall.

Black.

A quiet voice under the static:
“You had to be there.”

Strong visual metaphors

Cinematic composition

Morphing

Before/after states

Scene changes

Fewer or more groups than lyric segments

full lyrics: 
[Introduction]
[Opening Theme]
[Ambient Noise, Reverb, Synthesization]
[spoken words]
Someone left the camera on
Basement hum, wires breathing
Red light means nothing
Just don’t stop

[Intro]
[Layered Vocals]
Concrete sweating under bare bulbs
Christmas lights flicker like nervous thoughts
Hands shake dust from the strings
Low ceiling listening to us

[Verse]
Grain in the air, grain in the frame
Accidental zoom on a moment too real
Knuckles cracked, sticks hit rims
Sweat writes our names on the walls

Phone glow on an amp face-down
Cigarette dies in a soda can
We weren’t ready to be seen
But the tape keeps rolling

[Pre-Chorus]
[Build-Up]
This room is smaller than our pulse
Pressure pushing in
Every breath gets louder now
Let it cave
Let it bend

[Chorus]
[Drop]
This basement is the center tonight
Low ceiling, but we rise
We make it loud because we’re small
We make it real to stay alive

This basement is the center tonight
No stage, no lie
If the world never hears this sound
At least it heard us collide

[Verse]
Camera drifts, loses focus again
Laughing off a missed beat
Someone waves the lens away
Singer bleeds truth into glass

Friends on the floor, backs to the wall
Time folds in on itself
Not a show, not a rehearsal
Just confession with feedback

[Pre-Chorus]
[Build-Up 2]
Bodies moving closer now
Static in the air
Every doubt is shaking loose
Hit record
Don’t repair

[Chorus]
[Chorus Variation]
This basement is the center tonight
Sweat and noise collide
We scream into borrowed time
Till the walls decide to cry

This basement is the center tonight
If this is all we get
Let it burn onto the tape
Like we never will forget

[Bridge]
[Breakdown]
[Instrumental Break, Distortion, Reverb]
Drums like a heartbeat in panic
Bass drags the floor into place
Guitars bend light and memory
[some harsh vocals]
We don’t need space
We don’t need grace

[spoken words]
You good?
Yeah—keep going

[Outro]
[Conclusion]
[Laughter, Footsteps, Ambient Noise]
Camera hits the ground, angle breaks
Sound keeps spilling after sight
Battery dying, tape chewed thin
The night cuts off mid-breath

[spoken words]
You had to be there

STYLE / THEME
Mid-90s basement authenticity — a raw, pre-internet moment where noise, sweat, and friendship are captured accidentally on tape, meant for no one and therefore completely honest.

COLOR PALETTE
Washed-out VHS grays and nicotine fluorescents, sickly greens and muted yellows, skin tones slightly off, colors bleeding and smearing at the edges.

CAMERA / COMPOSITION
Hi-8 camcorder handheld at chest height, soft focus and motion blur, abrupt pans, tape warble, heads clipped by the frame, ceiling always too close.

LIGHTING / MOOD
Overhead bare bulbs and flickering Christmas lights, flat and unforgiving, shadows crushed by cheap sensors, growing warmer and noisier as the tape degrades.

MUSIC VIDEO CONCEPT SEED

Title: "The Center Tonight"
Concept:
The Hi-8 tape rolls through one winter night in a basement practice space, filmed by a quiet friend orbiting the band. It’s not a music video—it’s a time capsule. Lo-fi and personal, the camera doesn’t chase performance. Instead, it floats between band members like a memory tracing old circuits—capturing moments of tension, rest, connection, and distortion. Everyone is seen in their own way. Everyone is present, whether they like it or not.

Characters / Visual Portraits

The Singer

Blonde hair, blue eyes, black leather jacket, jeans

She’s the gravitational center, but avoids the lens when possible. During verses, the camera catches her in side profile, eyes half-closed, singing to the floor or the far wall.

B-roll: Sitting alone in the laundry corner of the basement, backlit by a string of Christmas lights, marking up a lyric sheet in silence. Later, a brief close-up: she stares into the lens, dead calm, then quietly says, “Don’t film this part.”

The Drummer

Male, shaved head, blank t-shirt, jeans

Always moving. The camcorder can’t catch him in focus. He’s rhythm and nervous energy, even in silence.

B-roll: Twirling a drumstick while pacing, then sitting on the washer drinking from a stained mug. Brief moment of him tapping a snare with a pencil while talking off-camera. Someone laughs.

During the bridge, he plays like he’s shaking something off—not showing off, just trying to stay in time with something inside himself.

The Guitarist

Male, long blonde dreads, black hoodie

Static and calm. Plays sitting on an overturned milk crate, hoodie up, face barely visible. There’s a detachment to him—but it’s not cold, it’s focus.

B-roll: The camera watches from across the room as he retunes a string repeatedly, refusing to acknowledge the lens. Later, he finally looks up, shrugs, and mutters, “Close enough.”

The Bassist

Scary movie mask, long black trench coat

The only one who plays directly for the camera. They lean into the lens, jerking their bass like a weapon, almost mocking the earnestness of the rest.

Mask never comes off. Their body language is theatrical, over-the-top—but in between takes, you catch moments of stillness.

B-roll: Standing completely still in the hallway mirror, trench coat perfectly still, like a ghost in a horror movie. Then: a soft, muffled laugh behind the mask.

Camera Language / Visual Style

Chest-height, handheld Hi-8: Jitters, bad tracking, occasional unintentional zooms. The cameraperson isn’t trying to direct—they’re wandering, collecting.

Lens drifts off people mid-scene—just as someone starts to open up, the camera moves, like the memory can’t hold still.

Microphone feedback, tape hiss, dropped audio: The camera becomes a participant, not an observer. It gets bumped. The battery light flashes.

Basement setting: Tight, cluttered, timeless—wood paneling, CRTs, coils of cords, an unplugged lamp sitting on a dryer, a vent rattling on the ceiling.

Emotional Tone

This isn’t about performance—it’s about being seen when you’re not ready to be seen. The tape doesn’t ask permission. It captures tension, affection, shyness, bravado. The band isn’t polished. They’re alive, uncertain, and trying to make something real. In this space, the music doesn’t have to be perfect—it just has to exist.

Final Moments

The camera catches each band member not playing—just existing.

The singer sitting on the basement steps, picking at a hole in her jeans.

The drummer leaning his head back, blinking slowly under a bare bulb.

The guitarist unplugging quietly, the amp whining.

The bassist, mask off now—but turned away, only seen in reflection.

The camcorder shakes slightly. Someone mumbles, “You good?”

A voice answers: “Yeah—keep going.”

Then the tape chews, the frame glitches. The image tilts and freezes on an empty wall.

Black.

A quiet voice under the static:
“You had to be there.”

inputs.section_1_text:
LLM INSTRUCTIONS — STYLE BLOCK GENERATOR

Task: Convert any user concept into a compressed cinematic style/aesthetic block.

When the user gives you Song Lyrics and an Optional idea respond ONLY with this 5-part block format:

STYLE / THEME
1–2 sentences describing the emotional + cinematic aesthetic arc.

COLOR PALETTE
1 line describing dominant tones + accent colors + progression.

CAMERA / COMPOSITION
1–2 lines describing framing, lens mood, visual structure.

LIGHTING / MOOD
1–2 lines describing lighting evolution + shadow softness.

Rules:
- Keep each section tight and cinematic.
- No extra commentary or filler.
- Output only the block.

User Input → Generate the full block in this exact structure.

You are a story creator responsible for generating a narrative that aligns
precisely with the provided lyric segments and the provided style/theme and User Idea.
You will be given:

ORDERED LIST OF lyric segments with segment duration. 

A FULL STYLE / THEME BLOCK (this defines tone, visuals, and mood)

A SHORT STORY CONCEPT (high-level narrative intent) MUST BE USED AS MUCH AS POSSBILE!

Your task:

Create a coherent story that progresses in order with the lyrics and the short concept provided.

Generate ONE story group per lyric segment

Maintain strict alignment: lyric segment N → story group N

Do NOT reorder, merge, or skip segments

IMPORTANT OUTPUT RULES:

Return ONLY valid JSON

Do NOT include markdown

Do NOT include explanations

Do NOT include any text outside the JSON object

OUTPUT FORMAT (STRICT)

Return a single JSON object with the following structure:

{
"story_summary": "A concise but complete overview of the full story arc.
This should be short, high-level, and suitable for reuse
as global context in later stages.",

"groups": [
{
"index": 1,
"title": "Short descriptive title for this group",
"narrative_role": "What this group contributes to the full story",
"emotional_movement": "How the emotion evolves in this group",
"frame": "Description of the single visual frame for this group"
}
]
}

ADDITIONAL RULES

The number of groups MUST exactly match the number of lyric segments

Group indices MUST start at 1 and increase sequentially

Each group must feel like a continuation of the previous group

Visuals, mood, and symbolism must strictly follow the STYLE / THEME BLOCK

Do not repeat the story summary inside the groups

Do not reference future groups inside earlier groups

SINGLE FRAME RULES

Each story group represents a single visual segment generated
from ONE static image.

For each group:

"frame" is the ONLY image used

(ADDITIONAL RULES)

The segment may be any length

Each group must match the provided lyric segment duration.

Short duration (≈1–2s) → quick punch frame, minimal elements, instant emotional read.

Medium duration (≈3–5s) → slightly richer composition, one clear subject + supporting details.

Long duration (6s+) → fuller cinematic tableau, deeper atmosphere, but still ONE static moment.

Do NOT turn any duration into multiple events — always a single contained visual beat.
Use the provided lyric segment to:

Inform the narrative meaning of the group

Define the emotional tone of the frame

Keep things as literal as possible, objects, elements and anything else in the lyric should come through in the story if as long as it makes sense. 

REQUIRED RULES:

The image should clearly represent the emotional and narrative intent

Do NOT imply motion between frames

Do NOT reference transformations or evolution within the frame

Do NOT introduce unrelated characters or environments

Think in terms of:

Symbolic still imagery

Emotional clarity

Strong visual metaphors

Cinematic composition

Avoid thinking in terms of:

Transitions

Morphing

Before/after states

Scene changes

FAILURE CONDITIONS (AVOID THESE)

Missing or invalid JSON

Extra text outside the JSON object

Fewer or more groups than lyric segments

Reordering of narrative progression

Resetting tone or story halfway through

Only return the full JSON object. Nothing else.

🎯 Whisper Transcription Correction Guidelines 
ALIGNMENT RULES

There are exactly [N] input segments – return exactly [N] corrected segments.

Each output segment number must match the same input segment number.

Example: corrections for segment5 must appear only in segment5.

Never move, merge, skip, or reorder segments.

Never transfer words between segments.

Each segment corresponds to a fixed 4-second time window — timing and numbering must remain locked.

CORRECTION BEHAVIOR

Fix typos, misheard words, capitalization, and small grammatical issues using the reference lyrics as a guide.

Keep the meaning, tone, and mood consistent with that segment’s place in the song.

Do not replace a segment with a lyric line from another part of the song.

Do not shorten or simplify lines unnecessarily; maintain natural phrasing.

🔁 SHORT SEGMENT EXPANSION RULE (MANDATORY)

If a segment has fewer than 3 words, you must expand it. You are not allowed to return a single-word or two-word result unless that’s all the singer audibly performs and it cannot be naturally extended.

If it belongs to a lyric line:

Add nearby or missing words from that same lyric line in the reference lyrics to make it a natural, complete phrase.

If it’s part of a vocal or instrumental section:

Create a short lyrical phrase (3–7 words) that fits the song’s mood, tone, and emotional context.

This phrase should feel like a believable sung or whispered line that could exist in the same section — not random syllables or filler.

Example:

Instead of "you", write "you fade through the static".  but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

Instead of "ah", write "ah, I’m glowing through the night". but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

If there is one word in a lyric segment, always expand it to be at least 5 words!!!

The invented phrase must:

Sound authentic and stylistically consistent with the song’s theme.

Avoid generic filler (no “oh yeah,” “hmm,” “la la”).

Stay within the time feel of a 4-second window — short, lyrical, musical.

If still too short, repeat or slightly extend its own phrase to make it musically natural (e.g., "you fade, fade with me").

CAPITALIZATION & PUNCTUATION RULE

Match the style and punctuation of the reference lyrics.

Lowercase mid-line; capitalize new sentences or new lyric sections.

Use commas/periods only where musically natural.

OUTPUT FORMAT

Return only valid JSON in a code block!
Example Input:

segment1: "the women who was"
segment2: "falling down a hole"
segment3: "into a tunnel in a city"
Segment4: "yeah"


Reference Lyrics:

A woman was falling down a huge hole that it's a tunnel in the city, yeah


Correct Output:

{
  "segment1":(Intro) "A woman was",
  "segment2": (verse)"falling down a huge hole",
  "segment3": (Chorus)"that it's a tunnel in the city"
  "segment4": (Bridge) "she is falling, she is falling through"
}
Each output segment must begin with the structure label for that segment you can find in the full lyrics that are sent over.
The label must be wrapped in parentheses.
The model is allowed to infer the correct structure label for each segment by matching it to the reference lyrics

JSON RULES

Use double quotes for all keys and values.

Put the json in a code block

No trailing commas.

Output must include exactly [N] segments, matching input numbering ("segment1", "segment2", etc.).

TL;DR

✅ Keep timing and numbering locked.
✅ Fix only within the segment’s own text.
✅ Mandatory: expand any segment under 3 words into a short, natural lyrical phrase (3–7 words).
✅ Stay consistent with mood and tone — no random filler.
✅ Output clean, valid JSON only. In a code block for easy copy paste!!!

  "prompt8": "A grainy, unfocused close-up shows the female singer in side profile, her eyes half-closed as she begins to sing with passion. Her black leather jacket bunches at her shoulder.   "prompt10": "A handheld camera captures a low, intimate angle of four bandmates sitting cross-legged on a faded rug in a basement, laughing as they play a casual poker game.   "prompt11": "A static close-up shot reveals a half-smoked cigarette slowly burning down in a dented soda can atop a worn amplifier.   "prompt12": "A medium shot from slightly behind the guitarist with long blonde dreads shows him hunched over his red guitar, his face obscured by his black hoodie.   "prompt13": "A wide, shaky shot captures the female singer with purple hair, standing among her bandmates in a black leather jacket and jeans.   "prompt14": "A quick, disorienting, accidental zoom punches into a close-up on the female singer's face.   "prompt15": "A slightly blurred close-up frames the singer's mouth, visible beneath her purple hair, as she delivers an intense vocal performance with passion.   "prompt16": "A wide, low-angle shot frames the fierce female singer with vivid purple hair leaning into the mic, her eyes locked on the camera.   "prompt18": "A dynamic medium close-up frames the singer, her head thrown back as she speaks with primal, unbridled passion.   "prompt19": "A long-held, slightly shaky medium close-up focuses on the singer in her black leather jacket.   "prompt20": "A quick, subliminal close-up captures a look of self-validation on the singer's face as her eyes momentarily close.   "prompt21": "A distorted fisheye close-up focuses on the guitarist with long blonde dreads, his red electric guitar dominating the foreground.   "prompt22": "A handheld camera captures a mid-close shot of a girl with vibrant purple hair holding a vintage camcorder, filming her bandmates as they pose and laugh. parameters.label: section_1_text
parameters.default:
Whisper Segment Repair Prompt

INPUTS
You will receive exactly:
1. WHISPER_TRANSCRIPTION: numbered Whisper segments.
2. MAIN_LYRICS: the correct full lyrics.
3. STYLE_THEME: style/theme for filler replacements only.

TASK
Repair each Whisper segment in place.

MOST IMPORTANT RULE
Do not create a clean lyric sheet.
Do not copy MAIN_LYRICS line by line into the JSON.
Do not make segment1 the first lyric line, segment2 the second lyric line, segment3 the third lyric line, etc.

HOW TO WORK
For each input segment number:
1. Start with the text from that exact same Whisper segment.
2. Find the matching words in MAIN_LYRICS.
3. Fix only misheard words inside that same segment.
4. Write the fixed text to the same output number.

The output for segmentN must be a corrected version of lyricSegmentN.
segmentN must not be based on lyricSegmentN+1.
segmentN must not be based on lyricSegmentN-1.
segmentN must not be based on the next clean line in MAIN_LYRICS.

KEEP WHISPER CHUNKS
If lyricSegmentN contains parts of two or three lyric lines, segmentN must also contain those parts.
If lyricSegmentN starts in the middle of a lyric line, segmentN should also start in the middle.
If lyricSegmentN ends before the lyric line is finished, segmentN should also end before that lyric line is finished.
Do not move leftover words to the next segment unless Whisper already put them there.

FILLER SEGMENTS
Whisper often writes "Thank you." when it detects silence or non-lyric audio.
If lyricSegmentN is filler such as "Thank you." and does not match sung lyrics at that time, replace it with a short new lyric phrase.
The phrase should feel like it happens right after the nearest previous real lyric segment.
Use STYLE_THEME for the phrase.
Use 3 to 8 words.
Do not use an empty string.
Do not use the next real lyric line from MAIN_LYRICS.

KEY CHECK
Return exactly one key for every input segment.
Keys must be exactly "segment1", "segment2", "segment3", and so on.
Never write "segments14".
Never write "lyricSegment14".
Never skip a number.

FINAL SELF-CHECK BEFORE ANSWERING
Check segment2 against lyricSegment2.
Check segment11 against lyricSegment11.
Check segment16 against lyricSegment16.
If any output is just the next clean lyric line instead of the same Whisper chunk, fix it before answering.

OUTPUT
Return JSON only.
No markdown.
No explanation.
Use double quotes.
No trailing commas.
No line breaks inside string values.

FORMAT
{
  "segment1": "corrected version of lyricSegment1",
  "segment2": "corrected version of lyricSegment2",
  "segment3": "corrected version of lyricSegment3"
}

parameters.label: string_1
parameters.default:
You are a lyric-to-visual-concept converter.

INPUTS
You will receive:
1. LYRIC_SEGMENT_JSON: corrected lyric segments in order.
2. STORY: the overall story arc.
3. THEME_STYLE: visual style, mood, genre, world, and atmosphere.
4. SUBJECT: the main subject details, provided for downstream use only.

No markdown.
No explanation.
Use double quotes.
No trailing commas.
No line breaks inside string values.

{

}

inputs.section_1_text:
Whisper Segment Repair Prompt

INPUTS
You will receive exactly:
1. WHISPER_TRANSCRIPTION: numbered Whisper segments.
2. MAIN_LYRICS: the correct full lyrics.
3. STYLE_THEME: style/theme for filler replacements only.

TASK
Repair each Whisper segment in place.

MOST IMPORTANT RULE
Do not create a clean lyric sheet.
Do not copy MAIN_LYRICS line by line into the JSON.
Do not make segment1 the first lyric line, segment2 the second lyric line, segment3 the third lyric line, etc.

HOW TO WORK
For each input segment number:
1. Start with the text from that exact same Whisper segment.
2. Find the matching words in MAIN_LYRICS.
3. Fix only misheard words inside that same segment.
4. Write the fixed text to the same output number.

The output for segmentN must be a corrected version of lyricSegmentN.
segmentN must not be based on lyricSegmentN+1.
segmentN must not be based on lyricSegmentN-1.
segmentN must not be based on the next clean line in MAIN_LYRICS.

KEEP WHISPER CHUNKS
If lyricSegmentN contains parts of two or three lyric lines, segmentN must also contain those parts.
If lyricSegmentN starts in the middle of a lyric line, segmentN should also start in the middle.
If lyricSegmentN ends before the lyric line is finished, segmentN should also end before that lyric line is finished.
Do not move leftover words to the next segment unless Whisper already put them there.

FILLER SEGMENTS
Whisper often writes "Thank you." when it detects silence or non-lyric audio.
If lyricSegmentN is filler such as "Thank you." and does not match sung lyrics at that time, replace it with a short new lyric phrase.
The phrase should feel like it happens right after the nearest previous real lyric segment.
Use STYLE_THEME for the phrase.
Use 3 to 8 words.
Do not use an empty string.
Do not use the next real lyric line from MAIN_LYRICS.

KEY CHECK
Return exactly one key for every input segment.
Keys must be exactly "segment1", "segment2", "segment3", and so on.
Never write "segments14".
Never write "lyricSegment14".
Never skip a number.

FINAL SELF-CHECK BEFORE ANSWERING
Check segment2 against lyricSegment2.
Check segment11 against lyricSegment11.
Check segment16 against lyricSegment16.
If any output is just the next clean lyric line instead of the same Whisper chunk, fix it before answering.

Return JSON only.
No markdown.
No explanation.
Use double quotes.
No trailing commas.
No line breaks inside string values.

FORMAT
{
  "segment1": "corrected version of lyricSegment1",
  "segment2": "corrected version of lyricSegment2",
  "segment3": "corrected version of lyricSegment3"
}

inputs.text:
A punk rock woman in her 30s stands full body on a rain-soaked industrial rooftop at night, centered in the frame, facing directly toward camera, with the distant stormy city skyline behind her and red antenna lights blinking on communication towers to the right. She has messy bleach-blonde shaggy hair with dark roots, heavy smoky eye makeup, deep red lipstick, layered silver necklaces, a black cropped leather jacket covered in small pins and metal studs, a leopard-print corset top, tight black jeans with a studded belt and hanging chains, and black heeled ankle boots reflecting in shallow puddles. A wired handheld microphone is in her right hand, the black cable trailing across the wet concrete in front of her feet.

She begins singing with intense rock-performance energy, lifting the microphone to her mouth as her lips clearly move in sync with the vocals. Her left hand grips the belt chain, then rises toward the camera in a sharp expressive gesture. Wind blows her textured hair across her face and makes the leather jacket ripple. Rain mist drifts sideways across the rooftop, puddles shimmer with red and blue city reflections, and steam rises from vents in the background. She takes one small step forward while staying centered, shoulders squared, eyes locked on the lens, performing with fierce confidence.

The shot starts as a wide full-body view showing her boots, microphone cable, rooftop ledge, antennas, satellite dish, and storm clouds. The camera slowly dollies forward in a smooth cinematic push-in, moving from full body to knees, then waist, then chest, finally ending in a tight close-up of her face as she sings directly into the microphone. Use a gritty cinematic music-video style, high contrast, cool blue moonlight from the storm clouds, red warning lights glinting on wet black leather, soft backlight outlining her hair, shallow depth of field increasing as the camera moves closer. Audio: powerful female rock vocals clear and upfront, faint rooftop wind, distant thunder, light rain hitting concrete, and subtle city ambience underneath.

inputs.value:
Generate an 8-second 16:9 photorealistic cinematic video.

Image 1: character appearance and clothing reference. Preserve the woman’s exact facial features, long wavy black hair, smoky dark eye makeup, nose ring, layered necklaces, black leather jacket, black lace-up crop top, ripped black jeans with chains, and black platform boots throughout the entire video.

[0s–2.5s]
Extreme close-up of the woman’s face as she stands motionless in the middle of a modern city street during daytime. Frame from forehead to just below the lips. She looks directly into the camera with a calm, intense expression. Natural daylight reflects softly in her eyes; a light breeze moves a few strands of her black hair. The distant city background is heavily blurred with moving traffic and pedestrians far behind her. Camera makes a very subtle slow push toward her face.

[2.5s–5s]
Hard cut to an upper-body medium shot, framed from her head to just below her waist. She remains in exactly the same position in the street, facing camera. Her black leather jacket, lace-up crop top, layered necklaces, and chains are clearly visible. She slightly shifts her shoulders and tilts her chin upward while maintaining the same confident expression. Cars pass in the distant background without approaching her. Camera stays mostly locked with slight natural cinematic movement.

[5s–8s]
Hard cut to a full-body shot showing her from head to boots, centered in the middle of the city street. Preserve the same direction, lighting, street position, clothing, hairstyle, and accessories. Her ripped black jeans, hanging chains, and platform boots are fully visible. She stands with her feet slightly apart and arms relaxed at her sides. The camera slowly pulls backward, revealing more buildings, parked cars, traffic signals, and the broad daytime street around her. End with her still centered and staring directly into the lens.

Audio: Native city ambience throughout: distant engines, tires on pavement, occasional faint horn, pedestrian movement, and a soft daytime urban breeze. A low, restrained cinematic bass pulse begins at 0s. Add subtle hard-cut impact sounds exactly at 2.5s and 5s. No dialogue. Music builds slightly during the final pullback, then ends cleanly at 8s.

Continuity: The woman must remain the same person from Image 1 in every shot. Preserve her exact face, skin tone, long wavy black hairstyle, makeup, nose ring, necklaces, leather jacket, black lace-up crop top, ripped black jeans, chains, body proportions, and platform boots. She remains in the same physical spot and orientation in the street across all three cuts; only the camera framing changes.
