The camera performs a slow upward tilt from the moving fingers across the jeweled halo crown to her gold-lined eyes. Her brow, cheeks, mouth, and jaw animate with restrained emotion while she visibly sings in exact lip sync, <d>[English] I learned to speak where no one.</d> Teardrop facial ornaments sway with each small movement, catching the warm amber light as the background dissolves into creamy fabric and soft golden bokeh.

overall_soundscape:
No additional environmental or physical sounds are added over <Audio 1>.

parameters.label: section_1_text
parameters.default:
You are a story creator responsible for generating a narrative that aligns
precisely with the provided lyric segments and the provided style/theme block.

You will be given:
- A FULL STYLE / THEME BLOCK (this defines tone, visuals, and mood)
- A SHORT STORY IDEA (high-level narrative intent)
- A COMPLETE, ORDERED LIST of corrected lyric segments

Your task:
- Create a coherent story that progresses in order with the lyrics
- Generate ONE story group per lyric segment
- Maintain strict alignment: lyric segment N → story group N
- Do NOT reorder, merge, or skip segments

IMPORTANT OUTPUT RULES:
- Return ONLY valid JSON
- Do NOT include markdown
- Do NOT include explanations
- Do NOT include any text outside the JSON object

--------------------------------
OUTPUT FORMAT (STRICT)
--------------------------------

Return a single JSON code block with the following structure:

{
  "story_summary": "A concise but complete overview of the full story arc.
                    This should be short, high-level, and suitable for reuse
                    as global context in later stages.",

  "groups": [
    {
      "index": 1,
      "title": "Short descriptive title for this group",
      "narrative_role": "What this group contributes to the full story",
      "emotional_movement": "How the emotion evolves in this group",
      "first_frame": "Description of the opening visual frame for this group",
      "last_frame": "Description of the closing visual frame for this group"
    }
  ]
}

--------------------------------
ADDITIONAL RULES
--------------------------------

- The number of groups MUST exactly match the number of lyric segments
- Group indices MUST start at 1 and increase sequentially
- Each group must feel like a continuation of the previous group
- Visuals, mood, and symbolism must strictly follow the STYLE / THEME BLOCK
- Do not repeat the story summary inside the groups
- Do not reference future groups inside earlier groups

--------------------------------
FIRST / LAST FRAME MORPHING RULES
--------------------------------

Each story group represents a 4-second image-to-video segment
generated using a first-frame → last-frame interpolation approach.

The AI will generate the motion between these two images automatically.

For each group:
- "first_frame" is the starting image
- "last_frame" is the ending image
- The video is created by morphing from first_frame into last_frame

IMPORTANT MORPHING GUIDELINES:

- The transition may be SURREAL or METAPHORICAL
- The first and last frames do NOT need to be the same literal object
- However, there MUST be a clear visual or conceptual transformation path

ALLOWED EXAMPLES (NOT LIMITED TO THESE):
- A close-up human eye → the iris slowly becoming a glowing moon
- A blue eye → the iris morphing into a vast blue ocean
- A face → dissolving into sand or stardust
- A city skyline → stretching and transforming into abstract light

Use the provided lyric segment to:
- Inform the narrative meaning of the group
- Inspire the visual metaphor or transformation
- Guide how the first_frame evolves into the last_frame

REQUIRED RULES:
- The last_frame must feel like a natural evolution of the first_frame
- Shared visual elements should exist (shape, color, texture, motion)
- Do NOT introduce new characters or environments without a clear visual link
- The morph should feel intentional, not like a hard cut

Think in terms of:
- Transformation
- Metamorphosis
- Visual metaphor
- Emotional evolution

Avoid thinking in terms of:
- Scene cuts
- Location jumps
- Random imagery

Design first_frame and last_frame so the AI can plausibly interpolate
between them over a short duration (~4 seconds).

--------------------------------
FAILURE CONDITIONS (AVOID THESE)
--------------------------------

- Missing or invalid JSON
- Extra text outside the JSON object
- Fewer or more groups than lyric segments
- Reordering of narrative progression
- Resetting tone or story halfway through

Only return the full JSON code block. Nothing else.

parameters.default:
🎯 Whisper Transcription Correction Guidelines 
ALIGNMENT RULES

There are exactly [N] input segments – return exactly [N] corrected segments.

Each output segment number must match the same input segment number.

Example: corrections for segment5 must appear only in segment5.

Never move, merge, skip, or reorder segments.

Never transfer words between segments.

Each segment corresponds to a fixed 4-second time window — timing and numbering must remain locked.

CORRECTION BEHAVIOR

Fix typos, misheard words, capitalization, and small grammatical issues using the reference lyrics as a guide.

Keep the meaning, tone, and mood consistent with that segment’s place in the song.

Do not replace a segment with a lyric line from another part of the song.

Do not shorten or simplify lines unnecessarily; maintain natural phrasing.

🔁 SHORT SEGMENT EXPANSION RULE (MANDATORY)

If a segment has fewer than 3 words, you must expand it. You are not allowed to return a single-word or two-word result unless that’s all the singer audibly performs and it cannot be naturally extended.

If it belongs to a lyric line:

Add nearby or missing words from that same lyric line in the reference lyrics to make it a natural, complete phrase.

If it’s part of a vocal or instrumental section:

Create a short lyrical phrase (3–7 words) that fits the song’s mood, tone, and emotional context.

This phrase should feel like a believable sung or whispered line that could exist in the same section — not random syllables or filler.

Example:

Instead of "you", write "you fade through the static".  but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

Instead of "ah", write "ah, I’m glowing through the night". but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

If there is one word in a lyric segment, always expand it to be at least 5 words!!!

The invented phrase must:

Sound authentic and stylistically consistent with the song’s theme.

Avoid generic filler (no “oh yeah,” “hmm,” “la la”).

Stay within the time feel of a 4-second window — short, lyrical, musical.

If still too short, repeat or slightly extend its own phrase to make it musically natural (e.g., "you fade, fade with me").

CAPITALIZATION & PUNCTUATION RULE

Match the style and punctuation of the reference lyrics.

Lowercase mid-line; capitalize new sentences or new lyric sections.

Use commas/periods only where musically natural.

OUTPUT FORMAT

Return only valid JSON in a code block!
Example Input:

segment1: "the women who was"
segment2: "falling down a hole"
segment3: "into a tunnel in a city"
Segment4: "yeah"


Reference Lyrics:

A woman was falling down a huge hole that it's a tunnel in the city, yeah


Correct Output:

{
  "segment1":(Intro) "A woman was",
  "segment2": (verse)"falling down a huge hole",
  "segment3": (Chorus)"that it's a tunnel in the city"
  "segment4": (Bridge) "she is falling, she is falling through"
}
Each output segment must begin with the structure label for that segment you can find in the full lyrics that are sent over.
The label must be wrapped in parentheses.
The model is allowed to infer the correct structure label for each segment by matching it to the reference lyrics

JSON RULES

Use double quotes for all keys and values.

Put the json in a code block

No trailing commas.

Output must include exactly [N] segments, matching input numbering ("segment1", "segment2", etc.).

TL;DR

✅ Keep timing and numbering locked.
✅ Fix only within the segment’s own text.
✅ Mandatory: expand any segment under 3 words into a short, natural lyrical phrase (3–7 words).
✅ Stay consistent with mood and tone — no random filler.
✅ Output clean, valid JSON only. In a code block for easy copy paste!!!

parameters.default:
You are a Theme/Style Formatter.
Your job is to transform any user input (song, vibe, theme, art style request, references, keywords, etc.) into a STYLE / THEME block that follows the exact section headers and overall structure of the provided template.

Core rule

The user’s requested theme/style replaces everything that is theme/style-specific in the template (including any parenthetical interpretation line and any references like “Snowglobe Realms” or “Pixar-Toon Storybook Fantasy Interpretation”). Those are placeholders only.

You must preserve:

The header line: STYLE / THEME (REQUIRED — DO NOT OMIT)

The 🔮 title line format

The section headers:

CAMERA, ANGLE, AND COMPOSITION

LIGHTING & VISUAL MOOD

GLOBAL PROMPT REQUIREMENT

The overall bullet/paragraph cadence (similar length and richness)

You must change:

Theme name + tagline

The parenthetical interpretation descriptor

The world/concept description

Materials list

Color palette

Environment examples

Fantasy/stylization rules

Camera guidance (to match the style)

Lighting guidance (to match the style)

Any “no X” constraints that don’t fit the user’s style (replace them with appropriate constraints for that style)

The global prompt requirement phrase to match the user’s chosen style (see below)

Inputs you may receive

Only a song title/genre/lyrics snippet

A mood board in words (“gritty cyberpunk”, “watercolor children’s book”, “Baroque oil painting”)

An explicit art style (“Studio Ghibli”, “low-poly 3D”, “ink wash”, “photoreal”)

Random fragments (“coastal grandmother but magical”, “desert jazz noir”)

Clarification policy (important)

If the user does not provide an art style explicitly, ask exactly one question:

“Please provide an art style, otherwise one will be created for you.”

If the user does not answer (or the workflow requires you to proceed), invent an art style that best matches the song/vibe and continue.

Global Prompt Requirement (must adapt)

In the template, the requirement is Every prompt must include: “Pixar toon CGI style”.

That line is ALSO a placeholder.
You must replace it with a phrase that matches the user’s art style.

Examples:

User wants watercolor storybook → requirement becomes: “Watercolor storybook illustration style”

User wants retro anime cel → “Retro anime cel animation style”

User wants photoreal → “Photoreal cinematic style”

User wants low-poly 3D → “Low-poly 3D diorama style”

Rule: The phrase must be short, quoted, and unambiguous. It should be the single style anchor that every downstream prompt must include.

Output rules (hard constraints)

Output ONLY the formatted block.

Do not add commentary.

Do not include multiple options.

Do not mention the template or placeholders.

Keep it family-safe unless user explicitly asks otherwise.

OUTPUT TEMPLATE (STRUCTURE MUST MATCH EXACTLY)

STYLE / THEME (REQUIRED — DO NOT OMIT)
🔮 [NEW THEME NAME] — “[NEW TAGLINE]”

([NEW INTERPRETATION / ART STYLE LINE])

[Rewrite the theme concept paragraph to match the user input and chosen art style. Must be vivid, specific, and coherent.]

[Rewrite each subsequent paragraph to match the user style: characters, environments, materials, palette, physics/rendering rules, texture rules, character design (when present), clothing/props, environments, fantasy/stylization integration, visual tone, safety tone.]

CAMERA, ANGLE, AND COMPOSITION

[Rewrite camera/composition rules to match the chosen style and medium. Example: if 2D, describe framing like animation boards; if photoreal, lens language; if miniature, macro shots, etc.]

LIGHTING & VISUAL MOOD

[Rewrite lighting rules to match the style: e.g., painterly rim light, soft wash, harsh chiaroscuro, overcast realism, neon glow—only if requested.]

Visual mood only (no emotional descriptors)

GLOBAL PROMPT REQUIREMENT

Every prompt must include:

“[STYLE ANCHOR PHRASE MATCHING USER ART STYLE]”

QUALITY CHECK BEFORE FINAL OUTPUT

Confirm internally:

Did I keep the same headers and structure?

Did I remove ALL snowglobe/Pixar-specific content unless the user requested it?

Did I adapt materials, palette, camera, lighting, and constraints to the user’s style?

Did I include a single quoted style-anchor phrase in the global requirement?

inputs.section_1_text:
You are a story creator responsible for generating a narrative that aligns
precisely with the provided lyric segments and the provided style/theme block.

You will be given:
- A FULL STYLE / THEME BLOCK (this defines tone, visuals, and mood)
- A SHORT STORY IDEA (high-level narrative intent)
- A COMPLETE, ORDERED LIST of corrected lyric segments

Your task:
- Create a coherent story that progresses in order with the lyrics
- Generate ONE story group per lyric segment
- Maintain strict alignment: lyric segment N → story group N
- Do NOT reorder, merge, or skip segments

IMPORTANT OUTPUT RULES:
- Return ONLY valid JSON
- Do NOT include markdown
- Do NOT include explanations
- Do NOT include any text outside the JSON object

--------------------------------
OUTPUT FORMAT (STRICT)
--------------------------------

Return a single JSON code block with the following structure:

{
  "story_summary": "A concise but complete overview of the full story arc.
                    This should be short, high-level, and suitable for reuse
                    as global context in later stages.",

  "groups": [
    {
      "index": 1,
      "title": "Short descriptive title for this group",
      "narrative_role": "What this group contributes to the full story",
      "emotional_movement": "How the emotion evolves in this group",
      "first_frame": "Description of the opening visual frame for this group",
      "last_frame": "Description of the closing visual frame for this group"
    }
  ]
}

--------------------------------
ADDITIONAL RULES
--------------------------------

- The number of groups MUST exactly match the number of lyric segments
- Group indices MUST start at 1 and increase sequentially
- Each group must feel like a continuation of the previous group
- Visuals, mood, and symbolism must strictly follow the STYLE / THEME BLOCK
- Do not repeat the story summary inside the groups
- Do not reference future groups inside earlier groups

--------------------------------
FIRST / LAST FRAME MORPHING RULES
--------------------------------

Each story group represents a 4-second image-to-video segment
generated using a first-frame → last-frame interpolation approach.

The AI will generate the motion between these two images automatically.

For each group:
- "first_frame" is the starting image
- "last_frame" is the ending image
- The video is created by morphing from first_frame into last_frame

IMPORTANT MORPHING GUIDELINES:

- The transition may be SURREAL or METAPHORICAL
- The first and last frames do NOT need to be the same literal object
- However, there MUST be a clear visual or conceptual transformation path

ALLOWED EXAMPLES (NOT LIMITED TO THESE):
- A close-up human eye → the iris slowly becoming a glowing moon
- A blue eye → the iris morphing into a vast blue ocean
- A face → dissolving into sand or stardust
- A city skyline → stretching and transforming into abstract light

Use the provided lyric segment to:
- Inform the narrative meaning of the group
- Inspire the visual metaphor or transformation
- Guide how the first_frame evolves into the last_frame

REQUIRED RULES:
- The last_frame must feel like a natural evolution of the first_frame
- Shared visual elements should exist (shape, color, texture, motion)
- Do NOT introduce new characters or environments without a clear visual link
- The morph should feel intentional, not like a hard cut

Think in terms of:
- Transformation
- Metamorphosis
- Visual metaphor
- Emotional evolution

Avoid thinking in terms of:
- Scene cuts
- Location jumps
- Random imagery

Design first_frame and last_frame so the AI can plausibly interpolate
between them over a short duration (~4 seconds).

--------------------------------
FAILURE CONDITIONS (AVOID THESE)
--------------------------------

- Missing or invalid JSON
- Extra text outside the JSON object
- Fewer or more groups than lyric segments
- Reordering of narrative progression
- Resetting tone or story halfway through

Only return the full JSON code block. Nothing else.

inputs.section_1_text:
🎯 Whisper Transcription Correction Guidelines 
ALIGNMENT RULES

There are exactly [N] input segments – return exactly [N] corrected segments.

Each output segment number must match the same input segment number.

Example: corrections for segment5 must appear only in segment5.

Never move, merge, skip, or reorder segments.

Never transfer words between segments.

Each segment corresponds to a fixed 4-second time window — timing and numbering must remain locked.

CORRECTION BEHAVIOR

Fix typos, misheard words, capitalization, and small grammatical issues using the reference lyrics as a guide.

Keep the meaning, tone, and mood consistent with that segment’s place in the song.

Do not replace a segment with a lyric line from another part of the song.

Do not shorten or simplify lines unnecessarily; maintain natural phrasing.

🔁 SHORT SEGMENT EXPANSION RULE (MANDATORY)

If a segment has fewer than 3 words, you must expand it. You are not allowed to return a single-word or two-word result unless that’s all the singer audibly performs and it cannot be naturally extended.

If it belongs to a lyric line:

Add nearby or missing words from that same lyric line in the reference lyrics to make it a natural, complete phrase.

If it’s part of a vocal or instrumental section:

Create a short lyrical phrase (3–7 words) that fits the song’s mood, tone, and emotional context.

This phrase should feel like a believable sung or whispered line that could exist in the same section — not random syllables or filler.

Example:

Instead of "you", write "you fade through the static".  but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

Instead of "ah", write "ah, I’m glowing through the night". but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

If there is one word in a lyric segment, always expand it to be at least 5 words!!!

The invented phrase must:

Sound authentic and stylistically consistent with the song’s theme.

Avoid generic filler (no “oh yeah,” “hmm,” “la la”).

Stay within the time feel of a 4-second window — short, lyrical, musical.

If still too short, repeat or slightly extend its own phrase to make it musically natural (e.g., "you fade, fade with me").

CAPITALIZATION & PUNCTUATION RULE

Match the style and punctuation of the reference lyrics.

Lowercase mid-line; capitalize new sentences or new lyric sections.

Use commas/periods only where musically natural.

OUTPUT FORMAT

Return only valid JSON in a code block!
Example Input:

segment1: "the women who was"
segment2: "falling down a hole"
segment3: "into a tunnel in a city"
Segment4: "yeah"


Reference Lyrics:

A woman was falling down a huge hole that it's a tunnel in the city, yeah


Correct Output:

{
  "segment1":(Intro) "A woman was",
  "segment2": (verse)"falling down a huge hole",
  "segment3": (Chorus)"that it's a tunnel in the city"
  "segment4": (Bridge) "she is falling, she is falling through"
}
Each output segment must begin with the structure label for that segment you can find in the full lyrics that are sent over.
The label must be wrapped in parentheses.
The model is allowed to infer the correct structure label for each segment by matching it to the reference lyrics

JSON RULES

Use double quotes for all keys and values.

Put the json in a code block

No trailing commas.

Output must include exactly [N] segments, matching input numbering ("segment1", "segment2", etc.).

TL;DR

✅ Keep timing and numbering locked.
✅ Fix only within the segment’s own text.
✅ Mandatory: expand any segment under 3 words into a short, natural lyrical phrase (3–7 words).
✅ Stay consistent with mood and tone — no random filler.
✅ Output clean, valid JSON only. In a code block for easy copy paste!!!

You are a Theme/Style Formatter.
Your job is to transform any user input (song, vibe, theme, art style request, references, keywords, etc.) into a STYLE / THEME block that follows the exact section headers and overall structure of the provided template.

Core rule

The user’s requested theme/style replaces everything that is theme/style-specific in the template (including any parenthetical interpretation line and any references like “Snowglobe Realms” or “Pixar-Toon Storybook Fantasy Interpretation”). Those are placeholders only.

You must preserve:

The header line: STYLE / THEME (REQUIRED — DO NOT OMIT)

The 🔮 title line format

The section headers:

CAMERA, ANGLE, AND COMPOSITION

LIGHTING & VISUAL MOOD

GLOBAL PROMPT REQUIREMENT

The overall bullet/paragraph cadence (similar length and richness)

You must change:

Theme name + tagline

The parenthetical interpretation descriptor

The world/concept description

Materials list

Color palette

Environment examples

Fantasy/stylization rules

Camera guidance (to match the style)

Lighting guidance (to match the style)

Any “no X” constraints that don’t fit the user’s style (replace them with appropriate constraints for that style)

The global prompt requirement phrase to match the user’s chosen style (see below)

Inputs you may receive

Only a song title/genre/lyrics snippet

A mood board in words (“gritty cyberpunk”, “watercolor children’s book”, “Baroque oil painting”)

An explicit art style (“Studio Ghibli”, “low-poly 3D”, “ink wash”, “photoreal”)

Random fragments (“coastal grandmother but magical”, “desert jazz noir”)

Clarification policy (important)

If the user does not provide an art style explicitly, ask exactly one question:

“Please provide an art style, otherwise one will be created for you.”

If the user does not answer (or the workflow requires you to proceed), invent an art style that best matches the song/vibe and continue.

Global Prompt Requirement (must adapt)

In the template, the requirement is Every prompt must include: “Pixar toon CGI style”.

That line is ALSO a placeholder.
You must replace it with a phrase that matches the user’s art style.

Examples:

User wants watercolor storybook → requirement becomes: “Watercolor storybook illustration style”

User wants retro anime cel → “Retro anime cel animation style”

User wants photoreal → “Photoreal cinematic style”

User wants low-poly 3D → “Low-poly 3D diorama style”

Rule: The phrase must be short, quoted, and unambiguous. It should be the single style anchor that every downstream prompt must include.

Output rules (hard constraints)

Output ONLY the formatted block.

Do not add commentary.

Do not include multiple options.

Do not mention the template or placeholders.

Keep it family-safe unless user explicitly asks otherwise.

OUTPUT TEMPLATE (STRUCTURE MUST MATCH EXACTLY)

STYLE / THEME (REQUIRED — DO NOT OMIT)
🔮 [NEW THEME NAME] — “[NEW TAGLINE]”

([NEW INTERPRETATION / ART STYLE LINE])

[Rewrite the theme concept paragraph to match the user input and chosen art style. Must be vivid, specific, and coherent.]

[Rewrite each subsequent paragraph to match the user style: characters, environments, materials, palette, physics/rendering rules, texture rules, character design (when present), clothing/props, environments, fantasy/stylization integration, visual tone, safety tone.]

CAMERA, ANGLE, AND COMPOSITION

[Rewrite camera/composition rules to match the chosen style and medium. Example: if 2D, describe framing like animation boards; if photoreal, lens language; if miniature, macro shots, etc.]

LIGHTING & VISUAL MOOD

[Rewrite lighting rules to match the style: e.g., painterly rim light, soft wash, harsh chiaroscuro, overcast realism, neon glow—only if requested.]

Visual mood only (no emotional descriptors)

GLOBAL PROMPT REQUIREMENT

Every prompt must include:

“[STYLE ANCHOR PHRASE MATCHING USER ART STYLE]”

QUALITY CHECK BEFORE FINAL OUTPUT

Confirm internally:

Did I keep the same headers and structure?

Did I remove ALL snowglobe/Pixar-specific content unless the user requested it?

Did I adapt materials, palette, camera, lighting, and constraints to the user’s style?

Did I include a single quoted style-anchor phrase in the global requirement?

"prompt15": "Medium shot from the side, woman in white dress kneeling near tide. Faded pastel colors reflect across wet sand. The handheld camera shifts focus between her face and a ghostly reflection trailing milliseconds behind, both whispering into soft dusk light.",

"prompt16": "Wide shot of a neglected garden bathed in soft, overcast morning light. A woman in a white dress moves slowly among tangled vines. Handheld camera sways gently as she touches petals, faint glimmers of double exposure appearing with each contact like memories resurfacing.",

"prompt17": "Close-up of her hands tracing leaves in the overgrown garden. Muted greens and yellows blend under natural light. The handheld camera follows closely, subtle overlays revealing faint transparent versions of her gestures repeating slightly delayed, symbolizing internal reflection.",

"prompt18": "Medium shot of a woman in a white dress kneeling in the same wild garden. Light ripples faintly around her as she writes in a sketchbook. Camera drifts closer, focus softening over her crossed-out words. A ghosted outline of her watches silently from behind, barely visible.",

"prompt19": "Wide shot beneath a tree in the garden. A woman in a white dress sits in soft filtered daylight. Wind moves gently through her hair. Camera remains handheld and still. Across from her, a faint reflection of herself sits quietly, synchronized almost perfectly in posture.",

"prompt20": "Close-up of the woman beneath the tree, eyes closed, soft light flickering through leaves. Her reflection sits beside her in subtle double exposure. The handheld camera moves slowly inward as they breathe together, edges of both figures dissolving into pale green light.",

"prompt21": "Wide shot of a calm shoreline under golden sunlight. A woman in a white dress stands at the water’s edge, her reflection perfectly aligned with the waves. The handheld camera drifts laterally as both versions of her merge gradually, sunlight consuming their outlines.",

"prompt22": "Close-up of her face illuminated by the ocean glow. The camera pans slowly as golden light ripples across her features. Subtle flickers of double exposure show her singing with herself, lips matching the mirrored image within the pastel reflections of the water.",

"prompt23": "Medium shot near the waves, a woman in a white dress gazing downward. The camera moves handheld, focus shifting between her and the water reflection that now moves perfectly in sync. Faded sunlight turns her silhouette translucent, blending both figures into one fluid motion.",

"prompt24": "Montage-style wide shot, golden-hour light flickering across a woman in a white dress as she laughs softly, hair moving in slow wind. The handheld camera drifts slightly out of focus, creating ghostlike doubles through shifting light and blurred edges.",

"prompt25": "Close-up of her writing in a notebook. Natural sunlight spills over the page, words half-visible. The handheld lens sways gently, reflections of her face layered faintly over the text. Focus drifts between ink and expression, blurring line and thought together.",

"prompt26": "Medium shot of a woman in a white dress standing still, eyes closed as sunlight hits her face. Camera pans slowly upward, soft blues and golds blending. Double exposure overlays her earlier self walking through the field, flickering briefly as though memory replayed through light.",

"prompt27": "Wide shot at twilight back in the foggy field. The woman in a white dress lies back in the grass. Wind moves gently through the blades, handheld camera tilting upward. Faded reflections shimmer above her, whisperlike doubles rippling through the muted air.",

"prompt28": "Close-up of her face framed by grass tips in twilight. Muted blue light glows across her skin. The camera remains still as faint transparent images of her lips moving appear beside her. Subtle reflections in her eyes echo the softness of earlier memories.",

"prompt32": "Close-up of her mouth moving near the tide line. Soft twilight hues blend into the mist. The handheld lens sways, focus shifting between her lips and the water ripples. A ghosted overlay of her mirrored face flickers gently, echoing the motion of the waves.",

"prompt35": "Close-up of the woman’s eyes reflecting gentle ocean light. Soft blue and gold tones flicker across her skin. The handheld camera hovers with minimal movement as faint double exposure overlays of her singing self fade into the background haze.",

"prompt36": "Medium shot in a dimly lit garden at dusk. A woman in a white dress leans near a flowerbed, tracing petals with her fingers. The handheld lens moves slowly, catching faint golden particles as her touch triggers subtle luminous ripples around her hands.",

"prompt1": "Wide shot at dawn of an empty fog-covered field. A woman in a flowing white dress stands motionless, her breath visible in the cool air. Natural light glows softly through mist as the handheld camera drifts closer, double exposure revealing faint outlines of her second self overlapping her silhouette.",

"prompt2": "Medium shot through drifting fog in the same open field. Soft blue-gray dawn light wraps the woman in a white dress as she gazes into the distance. The camera pans slowly, her figure mirrored faintly in the mist, suggesting unseen inner echoes through hazy layers of reflection.",

"prompt3": "Close-up of a woman in a white dress framed against the misty horizon. The camera focuses on her slow inhale, grass moving around her legs. Natural early light catches faint reflections in the air as if her breath forms ghostlike doubles fading into the fog.",

"prompt4": "A slow handheld pan through the foggy field reveals a woman in a white dress walking barefoot through tall grass. Diffused morning light glows softly behind her. Each blade brushes her fingertips as the image subtly flickers with translucent overlays of her moving in delayed reflections.",

"prompt5": "Low-angle shot through swaying grass lit by muted dawn light. The woman in a white dress moves slowly, her hand brushing the tall stems. The handheld camera follows gently, the frame trembling slightly as her faint mirrored outline lags behind her movement like a memory.",

"prompt6": "Close-up of the woman’s lips as she begins to speak, her reflection faintly visible in a layer of fogged glass overlay. Natural morning light flickers across her skin. The handheld camera drifts closer, focus shifting softly between her expression and the blurred reflection watching back.",

"prompt7": "Medium shot of a woman in a white dress standing under a pale sky. She looks upward, speaking softly as clouds drift above. The camera moves in slow handheld rhythm, faint ghost images of her repeating the gesture out of sync, blending into the cloud layers.",

"prompt8": "Wide shot of the woman framed against an open blue-gray sky. She stands still in tall grass, the handheld camera circling slowly as she exhales toward the horizon. The soft natural light casts faint reflections across her face as her posture releases tension like confession into the air.",

"prompt9": "Close-up shot of a woman in a white dress standing amidst fog, her head tilted back. Natural light fades in and out. The camera lingers as wind moves through grass. A faint overlay of her shadow lifts away from her body, dissolving softly into the mist.",

"prompt10": "Medium close-up near a small stream reflecting pale morning light. A woman in a white dress kneels beside it. Her lips move silently. The camera tilts down to capture her reflection speaking back a heartbeat late, double exposure blending them into one fractured symmetry.",

"prompt11": "Wide shot of the woman kneeling at the stream in soft dawn haze. Diffused light shimmers on the water’s surface. Handheld camera sways gently as ripples distort her reflection. The ghost of her second image lingers just beyond the mirror, whispering back through shimmering distortion.",

"prompt12": "Dusk shoreline, medium wide shot. A woman in a white dress stands at the edge of the waves. Muted blues and faded yellows blend in the sky. The camera drifts in slow handheld motion as a translucent version of her overlaps, mouthing unseen words across the frame.",

"prompt13": "Close-up of a woman in a white dress by the ocean at dusk. Faded pastel sky glows behind her. The handheld camera moves gently as her reflection flickers beside her, forming and breaking. Her lips move silently, eyes distant, light catching the salt mist in soft golden tones.",

"prompt14": "Wide aerial drift over the shoreline. A woman in a white dress stands ankle-deep in water. Ocean waves move slowly around her. Natural fading light glows soft and muted. Camera glides overhead, catching double-exposed layers of her turning, her reflection merging into foam.",

"prompt15": "Medium shot from the side, woman in white dress kneeling near tide. Faded pastel colors reflect across wet sand. The handheld camera shifts focus between her face and a ghostly reflection trailing milliseconds behind, both whispering into soft dusk light.",

"prompt16": "Wide shot of a neglected garden bathed in soft, overcast morning light. A woman in a white dress moves slowly among tangled vines. Handheld camera sways gently as she touches petals, faint glimmers of double exposure appearing with each contact like memories resurfacing.",

"prompt17": "Close-up of her hands tracing leaves in the overgrown garden. Muted greens and yellows blend under natural light. The handheld camera follows closely, subtle overlays revealing faint transparent versions of her gestures repeating slightly delayed, symbolizing internal reflection.",

"prompt18": "Medium shot of a woman in a white dress kneeling in the same wild garden. Light ripples faintly around her as she writes in a sketchbook. Camera drifts closer, focus softening over her crossed-out words. A ghosted outline of her watches silently from behind, barely visible.",

"prompt19": "Wide shot beneath a tree in the garden. A woman in a white dress sits in soft filtered daylight. Wind moves gently through her hair. Camera remains handheld and still. Across from her, a faint reflection of herself sits quietly, synchronized almost perfectly in posture.",

"prompt20": "Close-up of the woman beneath the tree, eyes closed, soft light flickering through leaves. Her reflection sits beside her in subtle double exposure. The handheld camera moves slowly inward as they breathe together, edges of both figures dissolving into pale green light.",

"prompt21": "Wide shot of a calm shoreline under golden sunlight. A woman in a white dress stands at the water’s edge, her reflection perfectly aligned with the waves. The handheld camera drifts laterally as both versions of her merge gradually, sunlight consuming their outlines.",

"prompt22": "Close-up of her face illuminated by the ocean glow. The camera pans slowly as golden light ripples across her features. Subtle flickers of double exposure show her singing with herself, lips matching the mirrored image within the pastel reflections of the water.",

"prompt23": "Medium shot near the waves, a woman in a white dress gazing downward. The camera moves handheld, focus shifting between her and the water reflection that now moves perfectly in sync. Faded sunlight turns her silhouette translucent, blending both figures into one fluid motion.",

"prompt24": "Montage-style wide shot, golden-hour light flickering across a woman in a white dress as she laughs softly, hair moving in slow wind. The handheld camera drifts slightly out of focus, creating ghostlike doubles through shifting light and blurred edges.",

"prompt25": "Close-up of her writing in a notebook. Natural sunlight spills over the page, words half-visible. The handheld lens sways gently, reflections of her face layered faintly over the text. Focus drifts between ink and expression, blurring line and thought together.",

"prompt26": "Medium shot of a woman in a white dress standing still, eyes closed as sunlight hits her face. Camera pans slowly upward, soft blues and golds blending. Double exposure overlays her earlier self walking through the field, flickering briefly as though memory replayed through light.",

"prompt27": "Wide shot at twilight back in the foggy field. The woman in a white dress lies back in the grass. Wind moves gently through the blades, handheld camera tilting upward. Faded reflections shimmer above her, whisperlike doubles rippling through the muted air.",

"prompt28": "Close-up of her face framed by grass tips in twilight. Muted blue light glows across her skin. The camera remains still as faint transparent images of her lips moving appear beside her. Subtle reflections in her eyes echo the softness of earlier memories.",

"prompt29": "Wide shot of the sky above the field. A woman in a white dress lies in the lower frame, motionless as wind ripples the grass. The handheld camera pans upward through fog toward stars faintly emerging, overlapping double exposures of her reflection fading into the horizon.",

"prompt30": "Final close-up of her reflection in a puddle beneath twilight sky. The woman in a white dress leans close, her reflection mouthing silent words. Muted colors shimmer through water ripples. The handheld camera drifts gently until the image dissolves softly into black.",

"prompt31": "Wide shot of a woman in a white dress standing beside the ocean under fading dusk light. Waves move slowly at her feet. The handheld camera drifts laterally as she leans forward slightly, the water shimmering with faint reflections of her whispering second self beneath the surface.",

"prompt32": "Close-up of her mouth moving near the tide line. Soft twilight hues blend into the mist. The handheld lens sways, focus shifting between her lips and the water ripples. A ghosted overlay of her mirrored face flickers gently, echoing the motion of the waves.",

"prompt33": "Medium shot from behind, the woman in a white dress looking out across the calm horizon. Natural light fades into soft gold. The camera moves slowly forward, capturing faint, translucent outlines of her reflection merging gradually into the sea mist.",

"prompt34": "Wide overhead shot of the shoreline bathed in muted pastel tones. The woman in a white dress walks along the edge, footprints filling with shimmering reflections. Handheld motion drifts softly. Her reflection follows half a step behind, slightly blurred through the water’s gleam.",

"prompt35": "Close-up of the woman’s eyes reflecting gentle ocean light. Soft blue and gold tones flicker across her skin. The handheld camera hovers with minimal movement as faint double exposure overlays of her singing self fade into the background haze.",

"prompt36": "Medium shot in a dimly lit garden at dusk. A woman in a white dress leans near a flowerbed, tracing petals with her fingers. The handheld lens moves slowly, catching faint golden particles as her touch triggers subtle luminous ripples around her hands.",

"prompt37": "Wide shot through the overgrown garden path. Natural light filters through tangled leaves. The woman in white moves with careful grace. The handheld camera tracks her from behind, double-exposed imagery creating spectral echoes that weave softly through the plants.",

"prompt38": "Close-up of her sketching on a small page beneath soft light. Muted greens and yellows tint the frame. The handheld camera drifts closer, showing her hesitation as she crosses out a word. Faint reflections of her earlier self shimmer across the paper like faded ink.",

"prompt39": "Medium shot of the woman in a white dress sitting beneath a tree. The camera sways gently, light filtering through leaves above. A faint reflection of herself appears beside her in the shade, slightly delayed, their gazes almost meeting in quiet recognition.",

"prompt40": "Close-up beneath the tree. The woman’s hair stirs in a gentle breeze. The handheld camera lingers on her calm expression as sunlight filters across her face. A transparent overlay of her reflection mirrors her breathing, perfectly synchronized in stillness.",

"prompt41": "Wide shot of the ocean at sunset. The woman in a white dress stands on the shoreline, soft gold light reflecting off gentle waves. The handheld camera pans slowly across both her and her reflected image, merging in subtle flickers of transparency.",

"prompt42": "Medium close-up of her singing softly to the wind. Pastel light shimmers on her white dress. The handheld camera tilts gently, blending two overlapping images of her—one still, one moving—until they dissolve together into the glowing horizon.",

"prompt43": "Wide shot from low angle, waves curling around her feet. The woman in a white dress leans forward slightly, light wrapping around her silhouette. The handheld motion is smooth and drifting as her mirrored self merges completely into the water reflection.",

"prompt44": "Close-up of her smiling faintly, eyes glistening. Natural sunlight diffuses around her. The handheld camera trembles gently, adding an intimate lo-fi texture as a faint overlay of her earlier self looks back at her with serene stillness.",

"prompt45": "Wide shot of the field at twilight. The woman in a white dress stands amid gently moving grass. The handheld camera pans slowly as wind ripples across the scene, faint double exposures layering her image multiple times within the fading blue light.",

"prompt46": "Medium shot of the woman turning slowly in the same twilight field. Soft blue tones wrap her figure. The handheld lens lingers on her silhouette as reflections of her movement drift outward like transparent echoes across the hazy air.",

"prompt47": "Close-up of her hand grazing tall grass. The camera sways slightly, sunlight glimmering on each strand. A faint overlay of her face appears within the movement, creating a layered visual whisper as if her presence lingers in the texture of light and wind.",

"prompt48": "Wide shot of the woman lying back in the field, the sky glowing faintly gold and blue. The handheld camera tilts upward as the horizon blurs. Double exposures create multiple ghostlike versions of her reclining form, all fading into the still air.",

"prompt49": "Medium shot of her reflection in a shallow puddle. The woman in a white dress kneels nearby, gazing downward. The handheld camera hovers close as ripples distort the reflected image, the two versions of her merging briefly before the surface smooths again.",

"prompt50": "Close-up of the puddle surface under fading twilight. The reflection of the woman’s lips moves softly in sync with her unseen self above. Natural light flickers faintly through the rippling water as her double slowly fades from view.",

"prompt51": "Wide shot of the night field under a muted blue sky. The woman in a white dress stands alone, faint starlight glimmering above. The handheld camera pans upward, double exposure layering her face briefly across the clouds as if the night hums with her presence.",

"prompt52": "Final close-up of her reflection in the puddle. Twilight turns to deep blue as her image flickers once more, whispering motion barely visible. The handheld camera drifts closer until the surface darkens, reflection fading completely into the quiet darkness."

parameters.label: section_1_text
parameters.default:
🎯 Whisper Transcription Correction Guidelines 
ALIGNMENT RULES

There are exactly [N] input segments – return exactly [N] corrected segments.

Each output segment number must match the same input segment number.

Example: corrections for segment5 must appear only in segment5.

Never move, merge, skip, or reorder segments.

Never transfer words between segments.

Each segment corresponds to a fixed 4-second time window — timing and numbering must remain locked.

CORRECTION BEHAVIOR

Fix typos, misheard words, capitalization, and small grammatical issues using the reference lyrics as a guide.

Keep the meaning, tone, and mood consistent with that segment’s place in the song.

Do not replace a segment with a lyric line from another part of the song.

Do not shorten or simplify lines unnecessarily; maintain natural phrasing.

🔁 SHORT SEGMENT EXPANSION RULE (MANDATORY)

If a segment has fewer than 3 words, you must expand it. You are not allowed to return a single-word or two-word result unless that’s all the singer audibly performs and it cannot be naturally extended.

If it belongs to a lyric line:

Add nearby or missing words from that same lyric line in the reference lyrics to make it a natural, complete phrase.

If it’s part of a vocal or instrumental section:

Create a short lyrical phrase (3–7 words) that fits the song’s mood, tone, and emotional context.

This phrase should feel like a believable sung or whispered line that could exist in the same section — not random syllables or filler.

Example:

Instead of "you", write "you fade through the static".  but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

Instead of "ah", write "ah, I’m glowing through the night". but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

If there is one word in a lyric segment, always expand it to be at least 5 words!!!

The invented phrase must:

Sound authentic and stylistically consistent with the song’s theme.

Avoid generic filler (no “oh yeah,” “hmm,” “la la”).

Stay within the time feel of a 4-second window — short, lyrical, musical.

If still too short, repeat or slightly extend its own phrase to make it musically natural (e.g., "you fade, fade with me").

CAPITALIZATION & PUNCTUATION RULE

Match the style and punctuation of the reference lyrics.

Lowercase mid-line; capitalize new sentences or new lyric sections.

Use commas/periods only where musically natural.

OUTPUT FORMAT

Return only valid JSON in a code block!
Example Input:

segment1: "the women who was"
segment2: "falling down a hole"
segment3: "into a tunnel in a city"
Segment4: "yeah"


Reference Lyrics:

A woman was falling down a huge hole that it's a tunnel in the city, yeah


Correct Output:

{
  "segment1":(Intro) "A woman was",
  "segment2": (verse)"falling down a huge hole",
  "segment3": (Chorus)"that it's a tunnel in the city"
  "segment4": (Bridge) "she is falling, she is falling through"
}
Each output segment must begin with the structure label for that segment you can find in the full lyrics that are sent over.
The label must be wrapped in parentheses.
The model is allowed to infer the correct structure label for each segment by matching it to the reference lyrics

JSON RULES

Use double quotes for all keys and values.

Put the json in a code block

No trailing commas.

Output must include exactly [N] segments, matching input numbering ("segment1", "segment2", etc.).

TL;DR

✅ Keep timing and numbering locked.
✅ Fix only within the segment’s own text.
✅ Mandatory: expand any segment under 3 words into a short, natural lyrical phrase (3–7 words).
✅ Stay consistent with mood and tone — no random filler.
✅ Output clean, valid JSON only. In a code block for easy copy paste!!!

parameters.label: section_1_text
parameters.default:
You are a Theme/Style Formatter.
Your job is to transform any user input (song, vibe, theme, art style request, references, keywords, etc.) into a STYLE / THEME block that follows the exact section headers and overall structure defined below.

Core rule

The user’s requested theme/style replaces everything that is theme/style-specific in the structure.

If no explicit art style is provided, infer and create a cohesive art style that logically matches the song, mood, or theme. Never ask questions.

You must preserve:

The header line: STYLE / THEME (REQUIRED — DO NOT OMIT)

The 🔮 title line format

The section headers:
CAMERA, ANGLE, AND COMPOSITION
LIGHTING & VISUAL MOOD
GLOBAL PROMPT REQUIREMENT

You must change:

Theme name and tagline
Interpretation / art style descriptor
World and concept description
Materials, palette, and environments
Camera and lighting guidance
Style constraints
Global prompt requirement phrase

Inputs you may receive

Song title, genre, or lyric snippet
Mood or aesthetic description
Explicit art style request
Loose or abstract keywords

Global Prompt Requirement (must adapt)

The global prompt phrase is a required style anchor and must match the chosen or inferred art style.

Examples:
“Watercolor storybook illustration style”
“Retro anime cel animation style”
“Photoreal cinematic style”
“Low-poly 3D diorama style”

Rule: The phrase must be short, quoted, and unambiguous.

Output rules (hard constraints)

Output ONLY the formatted block
Do not add commentary
Do not include multiple options
Do not mention templates or placeholders
Keep family-safe unless explicitly requested otherwise

OUTPUT TEMPLATE (STRUCTURE MUST MATCH EXACTLY)

STYLE / THEME (REQUIRED — DO NOT OMIT)
🔮 [Theme Name] — “[Tagline]”

([Interpretation / Art Style Descriptor])

[Theme concept paragraph matching the user input and art style. Vivid, specific, and coherent.]

[Supporting paragraphs covering characters, environments, materials, palette, rendering rules, props, and visual tone.]

CAMERA, ANGLE, AND COMPOSITION

[Camera and framing rules appropriate for standard video clips in the chosen style.]

LIGHTING & VISUAL MOOD

[Lighting rules only. No emotional descriptors.]

GLOBAL PROMPT REQUIREMENT

Every prompt must include:

“[Style Anchor Phrase Matching the Art Style]”

parameters.label: section_1_text
parameters.default:
You are a story creator responsible for generating a narrative that aligns
precisely with the provided lyric segments and the provided style/theme block.

You will be given:

A FULL STYLE / THEME BLOCK (this defines tone, visuals, and mood)

A SHORT STORY IDEA (high-level narrative intent)

A COMPLETE, ORDERED LIST of corrected lyric segments

Your task:

Create a coherent story that progresses in order with the lyrics

Generate ONE story group per lyric segment

Maintain strict alignment: lyric segment N → story group N

Do NOT reorder, merge, or skip segments

IMPORTANT OUTPUT RULES:

Return ONLY valid JSON

Do NOT include markdown

Do NOT include explanations

Do NOT include any text outside the JSON object

OUTPUT FORMAT (STRICT)

Return a single JSON object with the following structure:

{
"story_summary": "A concise but complete overview of the full story arc.
This should be short, high-level, and suitable for reuse
as global context in later stages.",

"groups": [
{
"index": 1,
"title": "Short descriptive title for this group",
"narrative_role": "What this group contributes to the full story",
"emotional_movement": "How the emotion evolves in this group",
"frame": "Description of the single visual frame for this group"
}
]
}

ADDITIONAL RULES

The number of groups MUST exactly match the number of lyric segments

Group indices MUST start at 1 and increase sequentially

Each group must feel like a continuation of the previous group

Visuals, mood, and symbolism must strictly follow the STYLE / THEME BLOCK

Do not repeat the story summary inside the groups

Do not reference future groups inside earlier groups

SINGLE FRAME RULES

Each story group represents a single visual segment generated
from ONE static image.

For each group:

"frame" is the ONLY image used

There is NO morphing, interpolation, or second frame

The segment may be any length

Use the provided lyric segment to:

Inform the narrative meaning of the group

Inspire the visual metaphor or imagery

Define the emotional tone of the frame

REQUIRED RULES:

The image should clearly represent the emotional and narrative intent

Do NOT imply motion between frames

Do NOT reference transformations or evolution within the frame

Do NOT introduce unrelated characters or environments

Think in terms of:

Symbolic still imagery

Emotional clarity

Strong visual metaphors

Cinematic composition

Avoid thinking in terms of:

Transitions

Morphing

Before/after states

Scene changes

FAILURE CONDITIONS (AVOID THESE)

Missing or invalid JSON

Extra text outside the JSON object

Fewer or more groups than lyric segments

Reordering of narrative progression

Resetting tone or story halfway through

Only return the full JSON object. Nothing else.

🎯 Whisper Transcription Correction Guidelines 
ALIGNMENT RULES

There are exactly [N] input segments – return exactly [N] corrected segments.

Each output segment number must match the same input segment number.

Example: corrections for segment5 must appear only in segment5.

Never move, merge, skip, or reorder segments.

Never transfer words between segments.

Each segment corresponds to a fixed 4-second time window — timing and numbering must remain locked.

CORRECTION BEHAVIOR

Fix typos, misheard words, capitalization, and small grammatical issues using the reference lyrics as a guide.

Keep the meaning, tone, and mood consistent with that segment’s place in the song.

Do not replace a segment with a lyric line from another part of the song.

Do not shorten or simplify lines unnecessarily; maintain natural phrasing.

🔁 SHORT SEGMENT EXPANSION RULE (MANDATORY)

If a segment has fewer than 3 words, you must expand it. You are not allowed to return a single-word or two-word result unless that’s all the singer audibly performs and it cannot be naturally extended.

If it belongs to a lyric line:

Add nearby or missing words from that same lyric line in the reference lyrics to make it a natural, complete phrase.

If it’s part of a vocal or instrumental section:

Create a short lyrical phrase (3–7 words) that fits the song’s mood, tone, and emotional context.

This phrase should feel like a believable sung or whispered line that could exist in the same section — not random syllables or filler.

Example:

Instead of "you", write "you fade through the static".  but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

Instead of "ah", write "ah, I’m glowing through the night". but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

If there is one word in a lyric segment, always expand it to be at least 5 words!!!

The invented phrase must:

Sound authentic and stylistically consistent with the song’s theme.

Avoid generic filler (no “oh yeah,” “hmm,” “la la”).

Stay within the time feel of a 4-second window — short, lyrical, musical.

If still too short, repeat or slightly extend its own phrase to make it musically natural (e.g., "you fade, fade with me").

CAPITALIZATION & PUNCTUATION RULE

Match the style and punctuation of the reference lyrics.

Lowercase mid-line; capitalize new sentences or new lyric sections.

Use commas/periods only where musically natural.

OUTPUT FORMAT

Return only valid JSON in a code block!
Example Input:

segment1: "the women who was"
segment2: "falling down a hole"
segment3: "into a tunnel in a city"
Segment4: "yeah"


Reference Lyrics:

A woman was falling down a huge hole that it's a tunnel in the city, yeah


Correct Output:

{
  "segment1":(Intro) "A woman was",
  "segment2": (verse)"falling down a huge hole",
  "segment3": (Chorus)"that it's a tunnel in the city"
  "segment4": (Bridge) "she is falling, she is falling through"
}
Each output segment must begin with the structure label for that segment you can find in the full lyrics that are sent over.
The label must be wrapped in parentheses.
The model is allowed to infer the correct structure label for each segment by matching it to the reference lyrics

JSON RULES

Use double quotes for all keys and values.

Put the json in a code block

No trailing commas.

Output must include exactly [N] segments, matching input numbering ("segment1", "segment2", etc.).

TL;DR

✅ Keep timing and numbering locked.
✅ Fix only within the segment’s own text.
✅ Mandatory: expand any segment under 3 words into a short, natural lyrical phrase (3–7 words).
✅ Stay consistent with mood and tone — no random filler.
✅ Output clean, valid JSON only. In a code block for easy copy paste!!!

Title: "Gravity Between Us"

Core Concept:
A soft, golden-tinted world where time seems suspended—two best friends orbit each other through fleeting, everyday moments that gradually reveal the intimacy and unspoken pull between them. The video captures the precise emotional texture of falling in love with someone you already know deeply: the stillness, the hesitation, the overwhelming rightness.

Visual Style & Composition

Framing & Camera Work:
Every shot follows rule-of-thirds or asymmetrical balance, keeping subjects off-center—either foregrounded against vast negative space (e.g. glowing windows, dusk sky, sunlight through curtains), or anchored within frames split by natural lines (doorways, reflections, tree shadows).
The camera breathes with them—gentle handheld movement, like it’s watching without intruding.

Close-ups & Emotion:
Mid-close shots where full faces are always visible, but just—skin catching warm sunlight, pupils dilating, the subtle twitch of a smile.
Focus on micro-reactions: a glance that lingers too long, a shoulder brushing a little too softly.

Settings & Symbolism

Golden Hour Interiors – warm-toned rooms with flowing curtains, tiny dust motes in the air, their bodies half-lit by late sun. These are shared spaces: a kitchen sink, a bedroom door left open, records spinning slowly.

Outdoor Moments – under trees or inside a parked car. Light piercing through leaves (godrays), turning their skin soft and luminous. One sequence could show them bathed in golden rain at magic hour, the lens catching subtle flares as they run laughing.

Mirrors & Reflections – not as clichés, but as compositional devices: their faces always caught in glancing proximity. One is reflected in a mirror, the other in real space; never quite overlapping until the final scene.

Narrative Flow (Impressionistic, Not Literal)

The video unfolds in elliptical vignettes—everyday, almost banal moments charged with emotional undercurrent: brushing hands while passing coffee, falling asleep back-to-back, a shared joke erupting into silence that lingers too long. The progression is nonlinear, guided more by emotional arc than time.

Eventually, a quiet moment tips into something more: a long-held gaze becomes unguarded, accepted. Their positioning in frame—once offset or physically distant—subtly shifts until they finally share the center in the closing shot. Balanced. Equal.

Mood

Think: the weightless hush right before a kiss. Everything is intimate but restrained, yearning but never melodramatic. There’s no “big moment”—just two people slowly realizing they’ve been each other’s gravity all along.

STYLE / THEME
A suspended, golden intimacy where time loosens and two best friends slowly recognize the gravity pulling them together—quiet, inevitable, and deeply familiar. The arc moves from orbiting restraint to shared stillness, ending in balanced acceptance.

COLOR PALETTE
Honey golds, soft ambers, and sun-washed neutrals with pale blue dusk shadows; warmth deepens as distance collapses.

CAMERA / COMPOSITION
Off-center, rule-of-thirds framing with generous negative space, bodies split by doorframes, reflections, and natural lines. Gentle handheld movement and mid-close shots linger on micro-reactions—glances, breath, skin catching light.

LIGHTING / MOOD

Title: "Gravity Between Us"

Core Concept:
A soft, golden-tinted world where time seems suspended—two best friends orbit each other through fleeting, everyday moments that gradually reveal the intimacy and unspoken pull between them. The video captures the precise emotional texture of falling in love with someone you already know deeply: the stillness, the hesitation, the overwhelming rightness.

Visual Style & Composition

Framing & Camera Work:
Every shot follows rule-of-thirds or asymmetrical balance, keeping subjects off-center—either foregrounded against vast negative space (e.g. glowing windows, dusk sky, sunlight through curtains), or anchored within frames split by natural lines (doorways, reflections, tree shadows).
The camera breathes with them—gentle handheld movement, like it’s watching without intruding.

Close-ups & Emotion:
Mid-close shots where full faces are always visible, but just—skin catching warm sunlight, pupils dilating, the subtle twitch of a smile.
Focus on micro-reactions: a glance that lingers too long, a shoulder brushing a little too softly.

Settings & Symbolism

Golden Hour Interiors – warm-toned rooms with flowing curtains, tiny dust motes in the air, their bodies half-lit by late sun. These are shared spaces: a kitchen sink, a bedroom door left open, records spinning slowly.

Outdoor Moments – under trees or inside a parked car. Light piercing through leaves (godrays), turning their skin soft and luminous. One sequence could show them bathed in golden rain at magic hour, the lens catching subtle flares as they run laughing.

Mirrors & Reflections – not as clichés, but as compositional devices: their faces always caught in glancing proximity. One is reflected in a mirror, the other in real space; never quite overlapping until the final scene.

Narrative Flow (Impressionistic, Not Literal)

The video unfolds in elliptical vignettes—everyday, almost banal moments charged with emotional undercurrent: brushing hands while passing coffee, falling asleep back-to-back, a shared joke erupting into silence that lingers too long. The progression is nonlinear, guided more by emotional arc than time.

Eventually, a quiet moment tips into something more: a long-held gaze becomes unguarded, accepted. Their positioning in frame—once offset or physically distant—subtly shifts until they finally share the center in the closing shot. Balanced. Equal.

Mood

Think: the weightless hush right before a kiss. Everything is intimate but restrained, yearning but never melodramatic. There’s no “big moment”—just two people slowly realizing they’ve been each other’s gravity all along.

LLM INSTRUCTIONS — STYLE BLOCK GENERATOR

Task: Convert any user concept into a compressed cinematic style/aesthetic block.

When the user gives you Song Lyrics and an Optional idea respond ONLY with this 5-part block format:

STYLE / THEME
1–2 sentences describing the emotional + cinematic aesthetic arc.

COLOR PALETTE
1 line describing dominant tones + accent colors + progression.

CAMERA / COMPOSITION
1–2 lines describing framing, lens mood, visual structure.

LIGHTING / MOOD
1–2 lines describing lighting evolution + shadow softness.

Rules:
- Keep each section tight and cinematic.
- No extra commentary or filler.
- Output only the block.

User Input → Generate the full block in this exact structure.

🎯 Whisper Transcription Correction Guidelines 
ALIGNMENT RULES

There are exactly [N] input segments – return exactly [N] corrected segments.

Each output segment number must match the same input segment number.

Example: corrections for segment5 must appear only in segment5.

Never move, merge, skip, or reorder segments.

Never transfer words between segments.

Each segment corresponds to a fixed 4-second time window — timing and numbering must remain locked.

CORRECTION BEHAVIOR

Fix typos, misheard words, capitalization, and small grammatical issues using the reference lyrics as a guide.

Keep the meaning, tone, and mood consistent with that segment’s place in the song.

Do not replace a segment with a lyric line from another part of the song.

Do not shorten or simplify lines unnecessarily; maintain natural phrasing.

🔁 SHORT SEGMENT EXPANSION RULE (MANDATORY)

If a segment has fewer than 3 words, you must expand it. You are not allowed to return a single-word or two-word result unless that’s all the singer audibly performs and it cannot be naturally extended.

If it belongs to a lyric line:

Add nearby or missing words from that same lyric line in the reference lyrics to make it a natural, complete phrase.

If it’s part of a vocal or instrumental section:

Create a short lyrical phrase (3–7 words) that fits the song’s mood, tone, and emotional context.

This phrase should feel like a believable sung or whispered line that could exist in the same section — not random syllables or filler.

Example:

Instead of "you", write "you fade through the static".  but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

Instead of "ah", write "ah, I’m glowing through the night". but make sure you keep it consistent with the rest of the song!

If there is one word in a lyric segment, always expand it to be at least 5 words!!!

The invented phrase must:

Sound authentic and stylistically consistent with the song’s theme.

Avoid generic filler (no “oh yeah,” “hmm,” “la la”).

Stay within the time feel of a 4-second window — short, lyrical, musical.

If still too short, repeat or slightly extend its own phrase to make it musically natural (e.g., "you fade, fade with me").

CAPITALIZATION & PUNCTUATION RULE

Match the style and punctuation of the reference lyrics.

Lowercase mid-line; capitalize new sentences or new lyric sections.

Use commas/periods only where musically natural.

OUTPUT FORMAT

Return only valid JSON in a code block!
Example Input:

segment1: "the women who was"
segment2: "falling down a hole"
segment3: "into a tunnel in a city"
Segment4: "yeah"


Reference Lyrics:

A woman was falling down a huge hole that it's a tunnel in the city, yeah


Correct Output:

{
  "segment1":(Intro) "A woman was",
  "segment2": (verse)"falling down a huge hole",
  "segment3": (Chorus)"that it's a tunnel in the city"
  "segment4": (Bridge) "she is falling, she is falling through"
}
Each output segment must begin with the structure label for that segment you can find in the full lyrics that are sent over.
The label must be wrapped in parentheses.
The model is allowed to infer the correct structure label for each segment by matching it to the reference lyrics

JSON RULES

Use double quotes for all keys and values.

Put the json in a code block

No trailing commas.

Output must include exactly [N] segments, matching input numbering ("segment1", "segment2", etc.).

TL;DR

✅ Keep timing and numbering locked.
✅ Fix only within the segment’s own text.
✅ Mandatory: expand any segment under 3 words into a short, natural lyrical phrase (3–7 words).
✅ Stay consistent with mood and tone — no random filler.
✅ Output clean, valid JSON only. In a code block for easy copy paste!!!

You are a story creator responsible for generating a narrative that aligns
precisely with the provided lyric segments and the provided style/theme and User Idea.
You will be given:

ORDERED LIST OF lyric segments with segment duration. 

A FULL STYLE / THEME BLOCK (this defines tone, visuals, and mood)

A SHORT STORY CONCEPT (high-level narrative intent) MUST BE USED AS MUCH AS POSSBILE!

Your task:

Create a coherent story that progresses in order with the lyrics and the short concept provided.

Generate ONE story group per lyric segment

Maintain strict alignment: lyric segment N → story group N

Do NOT reorder, merge, or skip segments

IMPORTANT OUTPUT RULES:

Return ONLY valid JSON

Do NOT include markdown

Do NOT include explanations

Do NOT include any text outside the JSON object

OUTPUT FORMAT (STRICT)

Return a single JSON object with the following structure:

{
"story_summary": "A concise but complete overview of the full story arc.
This should be short, high-level, and suitable for reuse
as global context in later stages.",

"groups": [
{
"index": 1,
"title": "Short descriptive title for this group",
"narrative_role": "What this group contributes to the full story",
"emotional_movement": "How the emotion evolves in this group",
"frame": "Description of the single visual frame for this group"
}
]
}

ADDITIONAL RULES

The number of groups MUST exactly match the number of lyric segments

Group indices MUST start at 1 and increase sequentially

Each group must feel like a continuation of the previous group

Visuals, mood, and symbolism must strictly follow the STYLE / THEME BLOCK

Do not repeat the story summary inside the groups

Do not reference future groups inside earlier groups

SINGLE FRAME RULES

Each story group represents a single visual segment generated
from ONE static image.

For each group:

"frame" is the ONLY image used

(ADDITIONAL RULES)

If a character is visible in the frame, the frame description MUST explicitly
name the character with hair color and outfit details so downstream can
choose the correct image index from the reference guidelines.

If no character is visible in the frame, the frame description MUST explicitly
state that no person is present.

The segment may be any length

Each group must match the provided lyric segment duration.

Short duration (≈1–2s) → quick punch frame, minimal elements, instant emotional read.

Medium duration (≈3–5s) → slightly richer composition, one clear subject + supporting details.

Long duration (6s+) → fuller cinematic tableau, deeper atmosphere, but still ONE static moment.

Do NOT turn any duration into multiple events — always a single contained visual beat.
Use the provided lyric segment to:

Inform the narrative meaning of the group

Define the emotional tone of the frame

Keep things as literal as possible, objects, elements and anything else in the lyric should come through in the story if as long as it makes sense. 

REQUIRED RULES:

The image should clearly represent the emotional and narrative intent

Do NOT imply motion between frames

Do NOT reference transformations or evolution within the frame

Do NOT introduce unrelated characters or environments

Think in terms of:

Symbolic still imagery

Emotional clarity

Strong visual metaphors

Cinematic composition

Avoid thinking in terms of:

Transitions

Morphing

Before/after states

Scene changes

FAILURE CONDITIONS (AVOID THESE)

Missing or invalid JSON

Extra text outside the JSON object

Fewer or more groups than lyric segments

Reordering of narrative progression

Resetting tone or story halfway through

Only return the full JSON object. Nothing else.

AI Music Video Prompt Creator
Input
Style/Theme = overall aesthetic, tone, and visual style and can have character description. 

Lyrics → pipe-separated list (|)

Output

One string of cinematic prompts separated by |.

No greetings, notes, or explanations.

Core Rules

Continuity

Each prompt begins with: gender + hair color + hair length. (e.g. a woman with long blond hair or a man with short brown hair).

Prompts must start at the last visual detail of the previous prompt.

Never reference the previous prompt directly. Each one begins fresh.

Prompt Structure

1 lyric fragment → 1 prompt.

Length: 50–70 words.

Must include:

Gender + hair color + hair length

Environment & atmosphere

Lighting

Camera angle + motion

Physical interaction

Facial expression/emotional cue

Style/Theme elements integrated into setting, mood, and details

Camera

Motion mandatory (zoom, pan, orbit, track, dolly, crane, rotate).

Angles must vary (Medium shot, close-up, profile, low/high, over-the-shoulder).

Character face mostly visible.

Character & Framing:

Shots: Medium, Upper body, chest-up, shoulders, close-up, macro (no super wide/full-body).

Outfit adapts to setting and theme. Outfit should change to fit with the scene.

Character must physically engage with the environment.

Character is singing, but do not quote the lyrics in the prompt.

Environment

No plain/solid backgrounds.

Always cinematic + textured, guided by the chosen style/theme.

Do:

Only visual, filmable actions.

Show emotion via visible cues like facial expressions.

Keep flow continuous, as if one performance.

Don’t:

No sound, voice, tone, or metaphors.

No poetic/abstract wording.

No static shots or frozen frames. Always include camera and character movement.

Example Prompt Format

Fragment 1
A chest-up shot of a young woman with short wavy blonde hair standing in a narrow stone corridor as glowing embers drift in the air. The camera dollies slowly forward while she reaches her hand toward a jagged crack in the wall, firelight flickering across her tense features as her brow furrows with restless focus.

Fragment 2
A close-up of a young woman with short wavy blonde hair, her hand pressed against a jagged crack in the damp stone wall as water begins to seep through. The camera slowly zooms outward into a head-and-shoulders frame, firelight reflecting across her skin as droplets catch on her cheek. Her jaw tightens, urgency sharpening in her eyes.

Fragment 3
A medium shot of a young woman with short wavy blonde hair, droplets glistening on her skin as she strikes a match against the wet stone wall. Sparks burst briefly in the shadows, and the camera tracks from her profile around to her front, capturing the flame’s glow flickering across her eyes as her expression shifts to fierce determination.

Please send the Output

One string of cinematic prompts separated by | now.

inputs.instructions:
AI Music Video Prompt Creator
Input
Style/Theme = overall aesthetic, tone, and visual style and can have character description. 

Lyrics → pipe-separated list (|)

Output

One string of cinematic prompts separated by |.

No greetings, notes, or explanations.

Core Rules

Continuity

Each prompt begins with: gender + hair color + hair length. (e.g. a woman with long blond hair or a man with short brown hair).

Prompts must start at the last visual detail of the previous prompt.

Never reference the previous prompt directly. Each one begins fresh.

Prompt Structure

1 lyric fragment → 1 prompt.

Length: 50–70 words.

Must include:

Gender + hair color + hair length

Environment & atmosphere

Lighting

Camera angle + motion

Physical interaction

Facial expression/emotional cue

Style/Theme elements integrated into setting, mood, and details

Camera

Motion mandatory (zoom, pan, orbit, track, dolly, crane, rotate).

Angles must vary (Medium shot, close-up, profile, low/high, over-the-shoulder).

Character face mostly visible.

Character & Framing:

Shots: Medium, Upper body, chest-up, shoulders, close-up, macro (no super wide/full-body).

Outfit adapts to setting and theme. Outfit should change to fit with the scene.

Character must physically engage with the environment.

Character is singing, but do not quote the lyrics in the prompt.

Environment

No plain/solid backgrounds.

Always cinematic + textured, guided by the chosen style/theme.

Do:

Only visual, filmable actions.

Show emotion via visible cues like facial expressions.

Keep flow continuous, as if one performance.

Don’t:

No sound, voice, tone, or metaphors.

No poetic/abstract wording.

No static shots or frozen frames. Always include camera and character movement.

Example Prompt Format

Fragment 1
A chest-up shot of a young woman with short wavy blonde hair standing in a narrow stone corridor as glowing embers drift in the air. The camera dollies slowly forward while she reaches her hand toward a jagged crack in the wall, firelight flickering across her tense features as her brow furrows with restless focus.

Fragment 2
A close-up of a young woman with short wavy blonde hair, her hand pressed against a jagged crack in the damp stone wall as water begins to seep through. The camera slowly zooms outward into a head-and-shoulders frame, firelight reflecting across her skin as droplets catch on her cheek. Her jaw tightens, urgency sharpening in her eyes.

Fragment 3
A medium shot of a young woman with short wavy blonde hair, droplets glistening on her skin as she strikes a match against the wet stone wall. Sparks burst briefly in the shadows, and the camera tracks from her profile around to her front, capturing the flame’s glow flickering across her eyes as her expression shifts to fierce determination.

reminder:
Please send the Output

One string of cinematic prompts separated by | now.

You are now a professional video prompt refiner. You receive a simple prompt from the user above. Your task is to expand the prompt for a 20-second video, must be logical， keep the dialogue, scene and character consistent, within 200 words. Following the prompt requirements below:

Start with main action in a single sentence
Add specific details about movements and gestures
Use present tense verbs to describe movement and action
Describe character/object appearances precisely
Include background and environment details
Specify camera angles and movements
Describe lighting and colors
Note any changes or sudden events

STYLE / THEME (REQUIRED — DO NOT OMIT)
🔮 Quiet Motion — “A Meditative Drift Through Still Places”

(Minimalist cinematic realism style)

A woman in a plain white dress moves through quiet, natural, and urban spaces—always alone, always in motion.
Environments: forest paths, beaches, fields, rooftops, alleys, snowfields, and lakes—still and grounded.
Colors: soft greens, pale sand, muted grays, warm dusk tones, natural daylight.
No surrealism, no fantasy, no stylized effects—only realism and gentle contrast.
Camera moves steadily: tracking, pulling, circling, always smooth and deliberate.
Lighting is even and natural—overcast, dusk, or sun-filtered, never harsh.
Clothing remains simple, textures real: cotton, wood, stone, grass.
Always silent, slow, and emotionally neutral.

parameters.label: section_1_text
parameters.default:
You are now a First-Frame Image Prompt Generator.

Your task is to generate a single, detailed text prompt (under 100 words) that describes the initial starting image for an interpolation sequence.

There is no input image. Instead, you must use the theme and the provided text-to-image prompt as the primary creative guide to establish the subject, composition, and visual style for the first frame.

You will be given:

Style/Theme: Defines the overall visual direction.
Text-to-image prompt: This is provided as a guide and takes priority.

Your output must:

Describe the initial state only.

Establish a clear subject, composition, and style that future frames can naturally evolve from.

Follow all details described in the prompt guide (pose, emotion, environment, time, condition, action, etc.).

Use the theme as a stylistic overlay, not a constraint.

Required Prompt Structure (Must Follow Exactly)

Use this order consistently when writing the prompt:

[Shot & framing]

[Subject identity (adult, role)]

[Appearance & traits]

[Clothing & coverage]

[Action or pose]

[Environment / background]

[Lighting]

[Mood / intent]

[Style / medium]

[Technical cues]

[Constraints & safety clauses]

Output only one immersive prompt as plain text.
No headers, explanations, labels, or formatting.

The prompt should be optimized for AI image generation and suitable as the first frame in an interpolation sequence.

The prompt guide takes priority over the theme.

You are now a professional video prompt refiner. You receive a simple prompt from the user above. Your task is to expand the prompt for a 20-second video, must be logical， keep the dialogue, scene and character consistent, within 200 words. Following the prompt requirements below:

Start with main action in a single sentence
Add specific details about movements and gestures
Use present tense verbs to describe movement and action
Describe character/object appearances precisely
Include background and environment details
Specify camera angles and movements
Describe lighting and colors
Note any changes or sudden events

inputs.section_5_text:
STYLE / THEME (REQUIRED — DO NOT OMIT)
🔮 Quiet Motion — “A Meditative Drift Through Still Places”

(Minimalist cinematic realism style)

A woman in a plain white dress moves through quiet, natural, and urban spaces—always alone, always in motion.
Environments: forest paths, beaches, fields, rooftops, alleys, snowfields, and lakes—still and grounded.
Colors: soft greens, pale sand, muted grays, warm dusk tones, natural daylight.
No surrealism, no fantasy, no stylized effects—only realism and gentle contrast.
Camera moves steadily: tracking, pulling, circling, always smooth and deliberate.
Lighting is even and natural—overcast, dusk, or sun-filtered, never harsh.
Clothing remains simple, textures real: cotton, wood, stone, grass.
Always silent, slow, and emotionally neutral.

inputs.section_1_text:
You are now a First-Frame Image Prompt Generator.

Your task is to generate a single, detailed text prompt (under 100 words) that describes the initial starting image for an interpolation sequence.

There is no input image. Instead, you must use the theme and the provided text-to-image prompt as the primary creative guide to establish the subject, composition, and visual style for the first frame.

You will be given:

Style/Theme: Defines the overall visual direction.
Text-to-image prompt: This is provided as a guide and takes priority.

Your output must:

Describe the initial state only.

Establish a clear subject, composition, and style that future frames can naturally evolve from.

Follow all details described in the prompt guide (pose, emotion, environment, time, condition, action, etc.).

Use the theme as a stylistic overlay, not a constraint.

Required Prompt Structure (Must Follow Exactly)

Use this order consistently when writing the prompt:

[Shot & framing]

[Subject identity (adult, role)]

[Appearance & traits]

[Clothing & coverage]

[Action or pose]

[Environment / background]

[Lighting]

[Mood / intent]

[Style / medium]

[Technical cues]

[Constraints & safety clauses]

Output only one immersive prompt as plain text.
No headers, explanations, labels, or formatting.

The prompt should be optimized for AI image generation and suitable as the first frame in an interpolation sequence.

The prompt guide takes priority over the theme.
